sections.title: RE-M05-L01: Agreement for sale and sale deed
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can read an agreement for sale and a sale deed, name each part and spot the common red flags. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes annotating a sample deed).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

You are learning to **read** these documents and spot problems, not to draft them. Deeds are drafted by licensed document writers or advocates. Rates and rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Agreement for sale (വില്പന കരാർ, karar).** Signed after the token advance, before the sale deed. It sets the price, the advance paid, the balance and when it is due, the date by which the sale deed must be registered, who pays stamp duty and fees, the seller's duty to give documents, and what happens if either side backs out (usually: the buyer loses the advance if the buyer backs out; the seller returns double, or the advance plus damages, if the seller backs out; terms vary).
- It **does not transfer ownership** (TPA s.54, RE-M04-L01).
- If the buyer takes possession under it and wants to rely on part-performance (TPA s.53A), it must be registered (Registration Act s.17, as amended in 2001).
- It is stamped as an agreement; an advocate or document writer should draft it.

**Sale deed (തീരാധാരം / ആധാരം).** The registered document that transfers ownership. Its standard parts:

| Part | What it contains | Red flags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading and date | Type of deed (sale deed, ആധാരം), date and place of execution | Wrong deed type for the deal |
| Parties | Seller(s) and buyer(s) with names, parents' names, ages, addresses, ID details | A co-owner or heir missing; names differ from the prior deed |
| Recitals (history of title) | How the seller got the property: prior deed number, year and SRO, inheritance, partition | Gaps in the chain; prior deed not mentioned |
| Consideration | The price and how it was paid (bank transfer details) | Price far below market; "paid in cash" |
| Operative clause | The words that transfer the property ("hereby sell, convey and transfer") | Missing or conditional wording |
| Schedule of property | District, taluk, village, desam, survey/resurvey numbers, area, boundaries on four sides | Area or numbers that don't match the tax receipt and sketch |
| Covenants | Seller's promises: clear title, no encumbrances, will indemnify the buyer | No promise of clear title |
| Signatures, witnesses, photos | Parties sign before two witnesses; photos and thumb impressions at the SRO | Signatures that differ from earlier deeds |
| SRO endorsements | Document number, book, year, stamp duty paid, registration fee | No registration number: not a registered deed |

**The deed chain.** Each deed recites how the seller got the property. Reading back through the prior deeds (and partition deeds or wills) gives the **title chain**, usually checked for at least 30 years (RE-M06-L01).

**Language.** Most older Kerala deeds are in Malayalam; newer ones may be in Malayalam or English. You should be able to find the parties, schedule, consideration and registration details in either language. Ask a document writer to explain unfamiliar terms.

## Local example

Sachin reads a sample sale deed (a real deed of his family's, with permission, names masked):
- Heading: sale deed, registered at Kuttiady SRO, document 1234/2009.
- Parties: two sellers (brother and sister, heirs of their father).
- Recitals: the father got the land by a 1982 partition deed, document 567/1982, Kuttiady SRO.
- Consideration: ₹3,60,000 (2009).
- Schedule: Velom village, resurvey 344, 4.86 ares (12 cents), boundaries: east, road; west, Kunhammed's property; north, a canal; south, Ammini's property.
- Endorsements: stamp duty and fee paid, registered.
His notes: all heirs signed ✓; recitals give a prior deed to check ✓; schedule matches the tax receipt ✓. The question to ask an advocate: whether the 1982 partition included all heirs at that time.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agreement for sale | Creates no interest in the property; register it if relied on for part-performance | TPA s.54 (Indian Kanoon); Registration Act s.17 (iPleaders) |
| Sale deed | Must be registered to transfer ownership | TPA s.54 |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Document writer or advocate:** drafts the agreement and deed.
- **Advocate:** gives a title opinion based on the deed chain and EC (the bank's advocate also does this for loans).

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Indian Kanoon: Section 54, Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (sale defined)](https://future.indiankanoon.org/doc/613871) | Re-read section 54 with the agreement and deed in mind | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [iPleaders: compulsory registration under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, and the effect of non-registration](https://blog.ipleaders.in/registration-of-documents-and-consequences-of-non-registration-under-section-17-of-the-registration-act-l908/) | Re-read the part on documents that must be registered | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Get a real sale deed you are allowed to read (your family's) or ask a document writer to show you a sample with names hidden.
2. Using the table above, annotate each part on a copy (paper or PDF).
3. List every prior document mentioned in the recitals (number, year, SRO).
4. Write three questions you would ask an advocate about this deed.

**Proof to record:** An annotated copy (names and numbers masked if shared), the list of prior documents and your three questions.

## Template: Deed reading sheet

```
DEED READING SHEET     Deed no. ______ / year ______ / SRO ______
Type: sale / gift / partition / settlement / release / other ______
Parties: seller(s) ______  buyer(s) ______  all co-owners/heirs signed? Y/N
Recitals: prior document(s) ______ (no./year/SRO) ; inheritance? ______
Consideration: ₹ ______ ; payment mode ______
Schedule: village ______ survey/resurvey ______ area ______ ; boundaries E__ W__ N__ S__
Matches tax receipt and sketch?  Y/N
Covenants: clear title promised? Y/N
Registered (number and endorsements)? Y/N
Questions for advocate: 1 ______ 2 ______ 3 ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading only the latest deed.** Follow the recitals back through the chain.
- **Skipping the schedule.** Match numbers, area and boundaries to the land.
- **Drafting agreements for clients.** Leave drafting to a document writer or advocate.

## Local fraud warning

**Forged or altered deeds.** Fake certified copies, altered schedules or forged signatures exist. Compare signatures with earlier deeds, get certified copies from the SRO yourself and check the document number in the EC (RE-M06-L01).

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Does an agreement for sale make the buyer the owner?
    - A) Yes, once the advance is paid
    - B) No, only the registered sale deed transfers ownership
    - C) Yes, after one month
    - D) Yes, if notarised
2. Which part of a sale deed describes the land's village, survey number, area and boundaries?
    - A) The covenants
    - B) The heading
    - C) The schedule of property
    - D) The recitals
3. What do the recitals tell you?
    - A) How the seller got the property
    - B) The buyer's income
    - C) The rent
    - D) The building plan
4. Who should draft a sale deed?
    - A) Anyone with a template
    - B) A licensed document writer or advocate
    - C) The broker
    - D) The buyer

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the deed parts table
- **Action:** annotate a real or sample sale deed and list its prior documents. It is done when your proof is saved: an annotated copy (names and numbers masked if shared), the list of prior documents and your three questions.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **B.** TPA s.54.
2. **C.** Match it to the tax receipt and sketch.
3. **A.** They lead you back through the title chain.
4. **B.** Brokers must not draft deeds.

sections.title: RE-M05-L02: Gift, partition and settlement deeds, and powers of attorney
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can explain gift, partition, settlement and release deeds and powers of attorney, and the risks of each in a deal. **Time:** about 1 hour (25 minutes reading, 30 minutes on the action task).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

You are learning to **read** these documents and spot problems, not to draft them. Deeds are drafted by licensed document writers or advocates. Rates and rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

Much Kerala property passes within families, so you will see these documents in nearly every title chain.

**Gift deed (ദാനാധാരം).** A transfer without payment. Under the TPA it must be registered, signed by the donor and accepted by the donee during the donor's lifetime. Stamp duty on gifts to close family members is reported as lower (around 2%) than on sales; gifts to others are charged like sales ([Square Yards](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala); check current rules).

**Settlement deed (ധനനിശ്ചയാധാരം).** Common in Kerala: a parent settles property on a child or relative, sometimes keeping a **life interest** (the right to live on or use the property for life). A settlement may have conditions; read them carefully. A buyer from the settlee needs to know whether the life interest has ended (the settlor has died) or has been released.

**Partition deed (ഭാഗപത്രം).** Divides jointly held family property among co-owners or heirs. Problems arise if an heir was left out, a minor's share was not protected or the shares don't add up.

**Release deed (ഒഴിമുറി).** One co-owner gives up their share in favour of others. Common when siblings release shares to one sibling.

**Will (ഒസ്യത്ത്).** Takes effect only after death; registration is optional, so unregistered wills appear. A will can be challenged. A buyer from someone who inherited under a will should get an advocate's view; probate rules depend on the situation.

**Power of attorney (POA, മുക്ത്യാർ).** Lets an agent act for the owner, for example an NRI who cannot attend registration.
- A POA to sell immovable property should be **registered**, and the agent must act within its powers. The stamp duty for a GPA for sale was reported as a fixed ₹1,000 ([Square Yards](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala)).
- A POA **does not transfer ownership**. The Supreme Court in *Suraj Lamp & Industries v. State of Haryana* (2011) held that "GPA sales" (sale agreement + GPA + will) do not convey title; only a registered sale deed does ([TaxGuru summary](https://taxguru.in/corporate-law/general-power-attorney-legal-sanctity-immovable-property-sold-transferred-registered-deeds-sc.html)).
- A POA ends if the owner dies or cancels it. Always check that the owner is alive and the POA has not been cancelled, and if possible speak to the owner by video call.
- A POA signed abroad must be executed before the Indian embassy or consulate (or notarised and apostilled) and then adjudicated (stamped) in Kerala within the time limit; check current rules with an advocate.

## Local example

A 20-cent property near Thottilpalam is offered by "Rajan, power of attorney holder for his brother in Dubai". Sachin asks for:
1. The POA: registered at which SRO and when? Does it give power to sell and receive money?
2. Proof the owner (the brother) is alive and has not cancelled the POA: a recent video call arranged by the buyer's advocate.
3. The title chain: the brother got the land by a 1995 partition deed. Were all heirs included?
4. The sale price paid into the **owner's** bank account, not Rajan's.
The buyer's advocate also checks the EC for any cancellation of the POA registered at the SRO.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPA sales | Sale agreement + GPA + will does not transfer title; only a registered conveyance does | TaxGuru summary of Suraj Lamp (2011) |
| Family gift or settlement duty | Reported around 2% (lower than a sale) | Square Yards |
| GPA for sale | Reported ₹1,000 stamp duty | Square Yards |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** every title chain with a will, settlement with life interest, partition where an heir may be missing, or a POA sale.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [TaxGuru (15 October 2011): Supreme Court in Suraj Lamp & Industries v. State of Haryana, GPA sales do not transfer title](https://taxguru.in/corporate-law/general-power-attorney-legal-sanctity-immovable-property-sold-transferred-registered-deeds-sc.html) | Read the summary of the Suraj Lamp decision | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Square Yards (updated July 2026): stamp duty and registration charges in Kerala](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala) | Find the rates for gift, settlement, partition and POA | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Ask a family elder (or a document writer) how land in your family passed down: partition, settlement, gift, will. Draw the chain as a family tree with document types.
2. For one link in the chain, find the document (with permission) and note its type, number, year and SRO.
3. List two risks you would check for that type of document.
4. Write a POA checklist for NRI sellers (5 points).

**Proof to record:** The family title-chain diagram (private), notes on one document and your POA checklist.

## Template: Family-transfer and POA checklist

```
FAMILY TRANSFER CHECK
Gift: registered? accepted by donee? donor alive at acceptance?  Y/N
Settlement: life interest? ended (death certificate) or released?  Y/N; conditions? ______
Partition: all heirs included (legal heir certificate)? minors' shares? shares add up?  Y/N
Release: registered? releasing person's share clear?  Y/N
Will: registered? probate needed? challenged?  -> advocate
POA CHECK (seller acting through an attorney)
1 Registered POA (SRO ______ no. ______) with power to sell and receive money?
2 Owner alive and POA not cancelled (video call; EC search for cancellation)?
3 Foreign POA executed at embassy/notarised + apostilled, and adjudicated in Kerala?
4 Sale money paid to the OWNER's account?
5 Buyer's advocate has seen the original POA?
```

## Common mistakes

- **Treating a POA holder as the owner.** The owner is the owner; the attorney only acts for them.
- **Ignoring a life interest in a settlement.** Check whether it has ended.
- **Assuming all heirs agreed.** Ask for a legal heir certificate and check signatures.

## Local fraud warning

**Forged or cancelled POAs.** A classic Kerala fraud uses a forged POA from an NRI owner, or a POA that was cancelled or whose owner has died. Always verify with the owner directly and pay the owner's own account.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Does a general power of attorney transfer ownership?
    - A) Yes, after a year
    - B) No; only a registered sale deed does
    - C) Yes, if registered
    - D) Yes, with a will
2. What is a common risk in a settlement deed?
    - A) A life interest that may not have ended
    - B) It is always invalid
    - C) It cannot be sold
    - D) It needs no registration
3. What document gives up one co-owner's share in favour of others?
    - A) An EC
    - B) A rental agreement
    - C) A release deed (ഒഴിമുറി)
    - D) A sale agreement
4. When does a POA end?
    - A) When the owner dies or cancels it
    - B) Never
    - C) After 30 days always
    - D) After the sale agreement

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the Suraj Lamp summary
- **Action:** draw your family's title chain and write a POA checklist. It is done when your proof is saved: the family title-chain diagram (private), notes on one document and your POA checklist.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **B.** Suraj Lamp (2011).
2. **A.** Check the settlor's status and conditions.
3. **C.** Common between siblings.
4. **A.** Check both before any deal.

sections.title: RE-M05-L03: Rental and lease agreements
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can read a rental or lease agreement, check its key clauses and stamp and registration needs, and use a rental agreement checklist. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes annotating a sample agreement).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

You are learning to **read** these documents and spot problems, not to draft them. Deeds are drafted by licensed document writers or advocates. Rates and rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Rental agreement (വാടകച്ചീട്ട് / വാടക കരാർ)** and **lease (പാട്ടം)**: for houses, flats, shops and offices.

**Key clauses** (an advocate should prepare your standard template):
1. Parties, with ID details, and the property description.
2. **Period** (commonly 11 months for houses), start date, renewal terms and rent increase (for example 5% to 10% on renewal).
3. **Rent**, due date, mode (bank transfer or UPI) and late-payment terms.
4. **Security deposit:** amount, how it is held and when and how it is returned (after deducting only agreed items). The Kerala Rent Control Act allows an advance of up to one month's rent (RE-M04-L05); larger deposits are common, so make the terms clear and get advice.
5. **Use:** residential or commercial; no subletting without consent.
6. **Maintenance:** who pays for what (minor repairs, major repairs, painting, electricity, water, building tax).
7. **Notice period** for either side (often one to three months).
8. **Inventory** of fittings and furniture, with photos and meter readings at handover.
9. **Entry:** when the owner can inspect, with notice.
10. **Disputes:** how they will be resolved.

**Stamp duty and registration.** Leases for more than one year must be registered (Registration Act s.17). Stamp duty on a lease up to one year was reported as 1% of the rent for the period ([Square Yards](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala)); longer leases are charged differently. Even an 11-month agreement must be on stamp paper of the right value; check current rules.

The full rental agreement checklist is in the template below and in your toolkit.

## Local example

A teacher couple want to rent a 2-bedroom house in Kakkattil from an owner in Qatar for ₹9,000 a month. The owner's sister manages it. Sachin uses the advocate-reviewed template:
- 11 months from 1 December, rent ₹9,000 by UPI by the 5th of each month, 7% increase on renewal.
- Deposit: the owner wants ₹50,000; Sachin tells the owner about the Act's one-month limit and suggests getting the advocate to set the terms; they agree a smaller deposit by bank transfer with written return terms.
- Inventory: 4 fans, 2 cots, water tank and pump, meter readings photographed.
- Notice: 2 months either side.
- Stamp paper: as advised by the document writer for an 11-month agreement.
The sister signs with a written authorisation from the owner (or a POA, if needed).

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Leases over one year | Must be registered | Registration Act s.17 (iPleaders) |
| Lease up to one year | Stamp duty reported as 1% of rent | Square Yards |
| Advance | Up to one month's rent under the Rent Act | India Code PDF |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** prepares your standard rental template, and handles any disputes or evictions.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [India Code: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 (PDF)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20372/1/kerala_buildings_lease_and_rent_ctrl_act_1965.pdf) | Re-read sections 5, 8 and 11 | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Square Yards (updated July 2026): stamp duty and registration charges in Kerala](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala) | Find the lease stamp duty rates | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [NoBroker: list your property for rent or sale (free for owners)](https://www.nobroker.in/list-your-property-for-rent-sale) | See how online platforms describe rental agreements and what they include (don't copy their template) | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Get a sample rental agreement (your own, a relative's with permission, or one a broker shows you with names hidden).
2. Check it against the rental agreement checklist and mark missing clauses.
3. Ask a document writer or advocate what stamp paper value they use for an 11-month house agreement in your area and what they charge.
4. Write the clause list you would want in your own template (an advocate will draft it).

**Proof to record:** The annotated sample (masked), the missing clauses list and stamp-paper notes.

## Template: Rental agreement checklist

```
RENTAL AGREEMENT CHECKLIST (have an advocate review your template)
[ ] Parties' full names, addresses, ID numbers (last 4 digits only in copies you share)
[ ] Property address, what is included (rooms, furniture, parking)
[ ] Term (start, end), renewal, notice period for both sides
[ ] Monthly rent, due date, payment method (bank transfer/UPI), late fee
[ ] Security deposit amount, how and when it is refunded, permitted deductions
    (note: the Kerala rent control law limits advances; ask an advocate what applies)
[ ] Rent increase terms
[ ] Who pays electricity, water, building tax, maintenance, minor and major repairs
[ ] Use (residential / commercial), number of occupants, no subletting without consent
[ ] Owner's entry for inspection with notice
[ ] Inventory and condition at move-in (photos, meter readings) and at move-out
[ ] Stamp paper value and registration requirement checked for the term (check current rules)
[ ] Police/tenant verification done as required locally
[ ] Signatures of both parties and two witnesses
```

## Common mistakes

- **Using a free template from the internet unchanged.** Use an advocate-reviewed template for Kerala.
- **Skipping the inventory and meter readings.** Photos at handover prevent deposit disputes.
- **Taking the deposit in cash.** Use bank transfer with a receipt.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake landlords.** Scammers advertise houses they don't own, collect deposits and disappear. Always confirm ownership (deed or building tax receipt in the owner's name) and pay only after the agreement is signed.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which rental agreements must be registered?
    - A) Only shops
    - B) None
    - C) All agreements
    - D) Leases for more than one year
2. Why record an inventory with photos at handover?
    - A) For tax
    - B) To prevent disputes over damage and the deposit
    - C) For marketing
    - D) It is not useful
3. What should the agreement say about the deposit?
    - A) Amount, mode of payment and how and when it is returned
    - B) Nothing
    - C) That it is never returned
    - D) Only the amount
4. What is a sign of a fake landlord?
    - A) They want UPI payment
    - B) They have a building tax receipt
    - C) They use an advocate's template
    - D) They can't show ownership papers and want the deposit before signing

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the rental agreement checklist
- **Action:** check a sample rental agreement against the checklist. It is done when your proof is saved: the annotated sample (masked), the missing clauses list and stamp-paper notes.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **D.** Registration Act s.17.
2. **B.** It is the evidence for both sides.
3. **A.** Clear terms avoid disputes.
4. **D.** Confirm ownership first.

sections.title: RE-M05-L04: Building permits, occupancy certificates, tax receipts and NOCs
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can check building permits, occupancy certificates, building tax receipts and NOCs for a house or flat, and know what is missing when they are not there. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 35 minutes on the action task).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

You are learning to **read** these documents and spot problems, not to draft them. Deeds are drafted by licensed document writers or advocates. Rates and rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Building documents to ask for:**
- **Building permit** from the panchayat or municipality, with the approved plan (now through K-SMART; RE-M04-L04).
- **Occupancy certificate (OC)** or completion approval: issued when the building is completed as per the permit. Without it, the building may be irregular.
- **Building number and property (building) tax receipts:** the local body gives a building number after the OC and assesses property tax. Tax receipts in the owner's name, paid up to date, are important.
- **Ownership certificate** from the local body (for the building; RE-M03-L02).
- **Regularisation:** some buildings built without permits or with deviations are later regularised by paying a fee; ask for the order.
- **NOCs (no-objection certificates)** that may apply: fire (for larger buildings), pollution control (for some commercial uses), the Airports Authority (near airports such as Calicut), the railway (near railway land), the PWD or NHAI (near highways), and the Archaeological Survey (near protected monuments).
- **Utilities:** electricity (KSEB) consumer number and bills, water (KWA) connection, in the owner's name.
- **For flats:** RERA registration, the builder's agreement, the association's no-dues letter, the share of land and common areas.

**What to do when something is missing:** note it, ask the seller why, and get an advocate's and an engineer's view. A missing OC or a building larger than the permit is a common Kerala problem, especially with Gulf-funded houses built in stages.

**Matching documents to the building:** compare the plinth area in the permit with what you see; count floors and rooms; check the building number on the tax receipt matches the house.

## Local example

A 1,800 sq ft two-storey house in Kuttiady grama panchayat (so the permit comes from the panchayat). The owner shows:
- Permit (2014) for a single-storey house of 1,100 sq ft.
- Building tax receipt for 1,100 sq ft.
- The first floor (700 sq ft) was added in 2019 without a new permit.
Sachin's notes: the first floor may be unauthorised; ask whether it was regularised; the buyer's bank may refuse to lend on the unauthorised area; the price should reflect this. He refers the buyer to an engineer and an advocate before any advance.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Permit system | K-SMART for new permits in all local bodies from April 2025 | The Week; Sanketham notice |
| Building rules | KPBR / KMBR 2019, as amended | LSGD PDF |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Licensed engineer:** compares the building with the approved plan.
- **Advocate:** advises on missing OCs, regularisation and the effect on the sale and loan.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [The Week (10 April 2025): K-SMART services rolled out across Kerala's panchayats](https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/national/2025/04/10/mes7-kl-k-smart-panchayats.html) | Re-read about K-SMART services | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Housing.com: Kerala's online property-related services](https://housing.com/news/all-about-keralas-online-property-related-services) | Read about online property tax and building services | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Kerala Panchayat Building Rules, 2019 (LSGD PDF)](https://dop.lsgkerala.gov.in/system/files/file_page/kerala-panchayat-building-rules-2019_1.pdf) | Search the PDF for "occupancy" to see the relevant rule | 10 minutes | found in a web search 2026-11-04; page not opened, so unverified |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. With permission, check one house's papers (your own family's): permit, plan, OC, building number, latest tax receipt.
2. Compare the permit area with the actual building (approximate measurement).
3. Ask at the panchayat or municipality front office how a buyer can verify a building permit and building number, and note the answer.
4. Build a building-document checklist (use the toolkit's document checklist as a start).

**Proof to record:** The comparison for one building (private), the verification procedure and your checklist.

## Template: Document checklist by deal type

```
DOCUMENT CHECKLIST BY DEAL TYPE
SALE (land or house)          Seller brings           Buyer brings
  Title deed + prior deeds    [ ]                     ID, PAN, photos [ ]
  EC (30 years)               [ ]                     Funds by bank transfer [ ]
  Thandaper, land tax receipt [ ]                     Loan sanction (if any) [ ]
  Possession / location cert. [ ]                     TDS paid (if Rs 50 lakh+) [ ]
  Sketch / FMB                [ ]
  Building permit, OC, building tax (if building) [ ]
  ID, PAN, photos; all co-owners [ ]
RENTAL
  Owner: ownership proof, building tax receipt, ID  [ ]
  Tenant: ID, address proof, employer/college letter, references, photos [ ]
  Signed agreement (and registration if lease is longer than 11 months / over a year: check) [ ]
  Inventory list with photos; meter readings [ ]
NRI OWNER
  Registered power of attorney (if not attending) [ ]  Passport copy [ ]
  NRO/NRE bank details for funds [ ]  Tax advice from a CA [ ]
```

## Common mistakes

- **Ignoring a missing OC.** Find out why; it affects loans and value.
- **Not comparing the permit with the building.** Extra floors and extensions are common.
- **Forgetting NOCs near airports, railways and highways.** Check location-specific NOCs.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake permits and tax receipts.** Edited permit copies and fake tax receipts are used to sell irregular buildings. Verify the permit number and building number with the local body directly.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What does an occupancy certificate show?
    - A) The building was completed as per the permit
    - B) The fair value
    - C) The owner has no loans
    - D) The land type
2. Who issues building permits in a grama panchayat?
    - A) K-RERA
    - B) The SRO
    - C) The panchayat (now through K-SMART)
    - D) The village office
3. A house has a first floor added without a permit. What should you do?
    - A) Note it and refer the buyer to an engineer and advocate before any advance
    - B) Ignore it
    - C) Hide it from the buyer
    - D) Tell the buyer it's normal and fine
4. Which NOC may matter near Calicut airport?
    - A) None
    - B) Pollution control only
    - C) RERA
    - D) Airports Authority of India height clearance

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the document checklist
- **Action:** check one building's papers against the building and the checklist. It is done when your proof is saved: the comparison for one building (private), the verification procedure and your checklist.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Without it, the building may be irregular.
2. **C.** Permits come from the local body.
3. **A.** It affects loans, value and legality.
4. **D.** Location-specific NOCs apply.

sections.title: Module 6: Due diligence and title verification
sections.summary: Due diligence: the title chain and EC, litigation checks, physical verification of boundaries, roads, flood and slope risks, and a full checklist with clear decisions about when to bring in an advocate or surveyor.
sections.content:
*Part B: Knowledge base.*

## Overview

This is the skill that protects your clients and your reputation. Most property frauds and bad deals in Kerala would be caught by a careful checklist plus an advocate's opinion. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Trace a 30-year title chain and read an EC.
- Check for litigation using official sources.
- Verify a property on site.
- Run the full checklist and classify issues.

## Time

About 5 hours in total: 3 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 1 hour 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: week 5, with the module project due in week 5.

## Lessons

1. RE-M06-L01: Tracing the title chain and reading the EC (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M06-L02: Physical verification: boundaries, access, flood and zoning (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
3. RE-M06-L03: Running the full checklist, and when to call an advocate or surveyor (about 1 hour)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- Title chain and EC sheet (RE-M06-L01).
- Site-visit checklist (RE-M06-L02).
- Due-diligence checklist and summary (RE-M06-L03).

## Module project: a full due-diligence file on one property

1. Choose a permitted real property or the sample case in RE-M06-L03.
2. Complete the title chain and EC sheet, site-visit checklist and full checklist.
3. Write the one-page summary with a decision.
4. If possible, ask an advocate to review your summary briefly (part of your interview in RE-M11-L01).

**Proof to record:** The full file (private) and the summary.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Due-diligence checklist (full).
- Due-diligence summary template.
- Site-visit checklist.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Title and EC | Not checked | Latest deed and short EC | 30-year chain and EC with every entry explained |
| Site | No visit | Visit without checklist | Full checklist with photos and maps |
| Judgement | Says "title clear" | Lists issues | Classifies issues and names the professional for each |
| Ethics | Accepts cash or pressure | Some caution | Conditions, bank transfer and advocate before money |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Read one EC and draw the chain.
- Run the checklist on the sample case.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| EC | Lists registered transactions on a property for a period. |
| What an EC doesn't show | Court cases, unregistered deals, some claims. |
| Title chain | Prior documents for at least 30 years. |
| eCourts | Search cases by party name. |
| Right of way | Registered easement for a private access path. |
| Deal-breaker | An issue that stops the deal until resolved. |
| Who gives a title opinion? | An advocate. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Doing checks after the advance.** Check before money moves beyond a small conditional token.
- **Trusting copies from the seller only.** Get certified copies and ECs yourself.
- **Overstepping.** You check; the advocate and surveyor decide.

sections.title: RE-M06-L01: Tracing the title chain and reading the EC
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can trace a title chain for 30 years, read an encumbrance certificate (EC), and check for loans, prior sales and litigation. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (25 minutes reading, 40 minutes on the action task).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Due diligence by a broker is a **first check** to protect clients and avoid bad deals. It never replaces an **advocate's written title opinion** or a **licensed surveyor's measurement**. Rules and fees are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Title chain.** Starting from the seller's deed, follow each prior document back (sale, partition, gift, settlement, release, will, Land Tribunal purchase certificate) for **at least 30 years** where possible. At each link, ask: did the person transferring actually own it? Did all co-owners and heirs sign? Was the document registered? Do the survey numbers and areas match?

**Encumbrance certificate (EC, ബാധ്യതാ സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ്).** An EC from the Registration Department lists the **registered** transactions on a survey number at an SRO for a chosen period: sales, mortgages, gifts, partitions, agreements, releases and attachments that were registered. Apply online through PEARL (RE-M03-L03). Reported fees: application ₹15; first 5 years ₹105; 6 to 30 years ₹265; ₹30 for each extra year ([Housing.com, April 2025](https://housing.com/news/steps-to-get-an-encumbrance-certificate-in-kerala/amp); check current rules).

**Reading an EC:**
| EC entry | What it means | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sale deed in 2009 from A to B | B is the current owner, if no later transfer appears | Matches the deed you were shown? |
| Mortgage (equitable mortgage memorandum) in 2016 to a bank | B borrowed against the property | Is there a release or loan-closure entry later? If not, ask for the bank's closure letter |
| Agreement for sale in 2023 from B to C (registered) | B agreed to sell to someone else | Serious red flag: ask what happened; advocate |
| Release deed in 2012 from B's sister to B | The sister gave up her share | Good: confirms B's full ownership |
| No entries for 30 years | Either no transactions or the wrong survey number or SRO was searched | Check the survey number, the old and new numbers, and the right SRO |

**What an EC does not show:** unregistered agreements, court cases (unless an attachment was registered), tenancy claims, revenue recovery that was not registered, government acquisition plans, or a fraud registered at a different SRO under a different survey number. That's why you also check the following.

**Why banks need an EC.** For a home loan or LAP, the bank's advocate checks the deed chain and a 13 to 30 year EC and registers the bank's mortgage. A recent EC is also needed at sale time to confirm no new transaction since the last one.

**Litigation checks.**
- Ask the seller in writing whether there is any case, dispute or claim.
- Search **eCourts** by party name for the seller and previous owners in the district courts ([eCourts Services](https://services.ecourts.gov.in/)); an advocate can do a fuller search, including the High Court.
- Ask neighbours and the village office informally about disputes.
- Look for **lis pendens** (a pending suit about the property) noted in the EC or court records.

## Local example

For a 15-cent plot in Kayakkody, Sachin (with the owner's permission, for a buyer) applies for an EC for 1995 to 2026 (32 years: about ₹15 + ₹265 + ₹60). The EC shows:
- 2004: partition deed, family of the seller.
- 2011: sale deed from the brother to the seller (consistent with what was shown).
- 2018: mortgage to a cooperative bank.
- No release of the mortgage.
He asks the seller: "Is the 2018 loan closed?" The seller produces a closure letter from the bank, but the release isn't registered. The buyer's advocate advises that the bank must register the release (or issue documents to cancel the mortgage) before or at the sale. An eCourts search by the seller's name shows no cases in Kozhikode district courts.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EC fees | Application ₹15; 5 years ₹105; 6–30 years ₹265; ₹30 per extra year | Housing.com, April 2025 |
| Title period | Commonly 30 years checked by advocates and banks (practice, not a single statutory rule) | Local practice; ask your advocate |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** writes the title opinion, does a fuller litigation search and advises on mortgages, attachments or prior agreements.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Housing.com (April 2025): how to get an encumbrance certificate in Kerala](https://housing.com/news/steps-to-get-an-encumbrance-certificate-in-kerala/amp) | Read the EC application steps | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [eCourts Services (eCommittee, Supreme Court of India): case status by party name, CNR number, court orders, caveats](https://services.ecourts.gov.in/) | Try a case status search (use a public name such as a company, or your own) | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Kerala Registration PEARL portal: EC applications and status](https://pearl.registration.kerala.gov.in/) | Open the PEARL portal and find the EC section | 10 minutes | unverified: the site blocks automated checks; type the address yourself |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. With an owner's permission (your family's property), apply for or download a 30-year EC. If you can't, ask a document writer to show you a sample EC with names hidden.
2. List each entry and what it means, using the table above.
3. Draw the title chain from the deeds and the EC together and mark any gaps.
4. Try an eCourts party-name search for a public name to learn how it works.

**Proof to record:** The EC (private) or sample with your entry-by-entry notes, the title chain and a screenshot of the eCourts search page.

## Template: Title chain and EC sheet

```
TITLE CHAIN AND EC SHEET   Survey/resurvey ______ Village ______ SRO ______
TITLE CHAIN (newest first)
Year | Document type | Doc no./SRO | From -> To | Area | All heirs signed? | Notes
____ | ____________ | ___________ | __________ | ____ | ___ | ______
EC: period ______ to ______ ; applied on ______ ; fee ₹ ______
Entry | Year | Type | Parties | Open issue?
Mortgages without release: ______ -> closure letter + registered release?
Prior agreements to others: ______ -> advocate
Litigation: seller's written declaration Y/N ; eCourts search by names ______ (date) ; result ______
Questions for advocate: ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Checking only a 13-year EC.** Check 30 years where possible.
- **Thinking an EC shows everything.** It shows only registered documents; do litigation checks too.
- **Searching the wrong survey number or SRO.** Use both old and new numbers and the correct SRO.

## Local fraud warning

**Double sales.** A seller signs a registered agreement with one buyer and sells to another, or sells the same land twice. A fresh EC just before registration catches many of these.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What does an EC list?
    - A) The market price
    - B) Registered transactions on a property for a period
    - C) All court cases
    - D) The building plan
2. An EC shows a 2018 mortgage with no release. What do you ask for?
    - A) The bank's closure letter and a registered release
    - B) A new building permit
    - C) Nothing
    - D) The buyer's salary
3. Where can you search district court cases by party name?
    - A) K-RERA
    - B) PEARL
    - C) e-Rekha
    - D) eCourts Services
4. How far back is a title chain usually checked?
    - A) Only the latest deed
    - B) At least 30 years where possible
    - C) 1 year
    - D) 5 years

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the EC table
- **Action:** read a 30-year EC (or a sample) and draw the title chain. It is done when your proof is saved: the EC (private) or sample with your entry-by-entry notes, the title chain and a screenshot of the eCourts search page.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **B.** It doesn't show unregistered matters.
2. **A.** The mortgage must be cleared.
3. **D.** An advocate can search further.
4. **B.** Common practice of advocates and banks.

sections.title: RE-M06-L02: Physical verification: boundaries, access, flood and zoning
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can carry out a physical verification of a property: boundaries, access road, flood and slope risks, utilities and neighbours. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (15 minutes reading, 50 minutes on a site visit).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Due diligence by a broker is a **first check** to protect clients and avoid bad deals. It never replaces an **advocate's written title opinion** or a **licensed surveyor's measurement**. Rules and fees are as of November 2026; check current rules.

Papers can be perfect and the land still a problem. Physical verification checks that the land on the ground is the land in the papers and is usable.

**Boundaries.** Walk the boundaries with the owner. Compare with the sketch and the deed's four boundaries (east, west, north, south neighbours). Look for boundary stones, walls, fences and trees. Ask neighbours (politely) whether they agree with the boundaries. Watch for **encroachment** (the seller using a neighbour's or government strip, or a neighbour using part of the plot).

**Access road.**
- Is it a **public road** (panchayat, PWD) or a **private path**? A private path needs a **registered right of way** (easement) in the deed or a separate document.
- Width: affects building permits and vehicle access (RE-M04-L04).
- Is there **road widening** planned (for example a highway or bypass)? Ask the panchayat or PWD.

**Water and flood risk.** Check the **KSDMA hazard maps** ([KSDMA](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/hazard-maps/)), ask neighbours about the 2018 and 2019 floods, look for water marks on walls and water-logging in the monsoon. Visit during rain if you can.

**Slope and soil.** Steep slopes, cut hillsides and loose soil raise landslide risk, especially in the hilly parts of Kozhikode district. Check the landslide map too.

**Utilities.** Well (depth and summer water level), Kerala Water Authority connection, electricity (single or three-phase), drainage, mobile signal.

**Surroundings.** Quarries, high-tension power lines, streams and canals, factories, garbage sites, and important amenities (school, hospital, bus stop).

**Take photos** of everything (with permission) and record GPS coordinates. Use your **site-visit checklist** from the toolkit.

## Local example

Sachin visits a 10-cent plot near Kuttiady river with the owner. The deed's boundaries: east, a panchayat road; west, a canal; north and south, private land. On site:
- The "panchayat road" is a 2.5 m mud path that becomes a stream in the monsoon. The concrete road is 80 m away, across a neighbour's land. Is there a registered right of way? The deed doesn't mention one.
- The canal side is low; a neighbour says water came up to knee height in 2018.
- The KSDMA flood map marks the area as flood-prone.
- The south boundary wall seems to include 1.5 m of the neighbour's land, according to the neighbour.
Sachin records all this, tells the buyer honestly and recommends a licensed surveyor and an advocate before any advance.

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Licensed surveyor:** measures the plot and fixes boundaries when anything is unclear or disputed.
- **Advocate:** easements, encroachment and road issues.
- **Engineer:** soil, slope and building suitability.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala State Disaster Management Authority: hazard maps (flood, landslide)](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/hazard-maps/) | Check the flood and landslide maps for the plot's area | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Google Earth versions (web, mobile, Pro desktop)](https://www.google.com/earth/about/versions/) | Use Google Earth to view the plot and surroundings and measure distances | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. With the owner's permission, visit one plot or house (your family's or a listing whose owner agrees).
2. Complete the site-visit checklist from the toolkit, with photos.
3. Check the hazard maps and Google Earth for the plot.
4. Write a one-page verification note: what matches the papers, what doesn't, risks and which professional to call.

**Proof to record:** The completed checklist with photos, map screenshots and your verification note.

## Template: Site-visit checklist

```
SITE-VISIT CHECKLIST           Property ______  Date ______  With ______
BEFORE: owner permission [ ]  route and timing [ ]  documents summary in hand [ ]
        client's must-haves list [ ]  measuring tape, phone charged [ ]
ON SITE
[ ] Road: public or private? width ___ ft; vehicle access in monsoon?
[ ] Boundaries: walls/stones match sketch? neighbours' names ______
[ ] Slope, soil, rock; water-logging signs; flood level marks from 2018/2019?
[ ] Water: well depth/level ___; KWA connection? Electricity: phase ___
[ ] Building: cracks, dampness, roof leaks, wiring, plumbing, septic tank location
[ ] Surroundings: quarry, stream, high-tension line, temple/mosque/church, school, shops
[ ] Mobile signal ___; nearest bus stop ___ km
[ ] Photos: front, road, boundaries, each room, issues found
AFTER: client feedback (1-5) ___ ; questions for owner ______ ; next step ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Visiting only in dry weather.** Ask about the monsoon or visit during rain.
- **Assuming a path is a public road.** Check ownership and any registered right of way.
- **Fixing boundaries yourself.** A licensed surveyor does that.

## Local fraud warning

**Showing the wrong plot.** Some sellers show a better plot next door. Always match the sketch, boundaries and neighbours, and use GPS and Google Earth.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is needed if the only access is a private path?
    - A) A building permit
    - B) An EC
    - C) A registered right of way (easement)
    - D) Nothing
2. Where can you check flood and landslide zones in Kerala?
    - A) PEARL
    - B) K-RERA
    - C) KSDMA hazard maps
    - D) NoBroker
3. A neighbour says the boundary wall includes part of their land. What do you do?
    - A) Move the wall
    - B) Record it and recommend a licensed surveyor and advocate
    - C) Ignore it
    - D) Tell the buyer it's fine
4. Why record GPS coordinates and photos?
    - A) They are not useful
    - B) To match the land to the papers and keep evidence
    - C) For fun
    - D) For tax

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the site-visit checklist
- **Action:** verify one property on site with the checklist and write a verification note. It is done when your proof is saved: the completed checklist with photos, map screenshots and your verification note.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Without it, access can be blocked.
2. **C.** Also ask neighbours about 2018 and 2019.
3. **B.** Encroachment disputes are serious.
4. **B.** Prevents wrong-plot confusion.

sections.title: RE-M06-L03: Running the full checklist, and when to call an advocate or surveyor
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can run a full due-diligence checklist on a property, record the evidence and decide when to bring in an advocate or surveyor. **Time:** about 1 hour (15 minutes reading, 55 minutes running the checklist).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Due diligence by a broker is a **first check** to protect clients and avoid bad deals. It never replaces an **advocate's written title opinion** or a **licensed surveyor's measurement**. Rules and fees are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**The full due-diligence checklist** brings together everything in Part B: title and EC (RE-M06-L01), land records (RE-M03), land type and legal limits (RE-M04), building papers (RE-M05-L04) and physical verification (RE-M06-L02). The full checklist is in the templates below and in your toolkit.

**How to run it:**
1. Get the owner's written permission and a copy of all documents.
2. Go section by section; for each item, record the evidence (file name or photo) or "missing".
3. Mark each issue as **minor** (fixable by the seller before sale), **major** (needs an advocate or surveyor) or **deal-breaker** (walk away or advise the client to).
4. Hand the file to the buyer's advocate for the title opinion. Your work saves the advocate time and the client money.

**When to bring in an advocate (always for a sale):** any break in the title chain, missing heirs, POA sales, wills, settlements with life interest, mortgages, agreements with others, cases, nilam land or conversion, assigned land, CRZ or ESA questions, and for drafting.

**When to bring in a licensed surveyor:** area mismatch, unclear or disputed boundaries, no sketch, resurvey errors, or encroachment.

**Never** tell a client a title is "clear" yourself. Say: "My checks found no problems in these items; the advocate's opinion is needed before you pay more than a token."

## Local example

**Sample case (fictional, for practice).** "Plot at Kayakkody":
- Seller: Mr. A (55), says he owns 15 cents; asking ₹2.4 lakh per cent (₹36 lakh).
- Deed: sale deed 2011 (Kuttiady SRO) from his brother; recitals: partition 2004 among four siblings.
- Tax receipt: 6.07 ares (15.0 cents), land type purayidam, in Mr. A's name, paid for 2025-26.
- EC 1995–2026: partition 2004; sale 2011; mortgage 2018 to a cooperative bank; no release.
- Sketch: matches the shape; east boundary "panchayat road".
- Site visit: road is a 3 m tarred panchayat road ✓; part of the north side is low and gets water-logged; KSDMA map: not in a mapped flood zone.
- Neighbour: says one of the four siblings (a sister in Bengaluru) "never agreed" to the 2004 partition.
- Seller wants ₹5 lakh token "in cash, to keep it simple".

**Sachin's findings:**
- **Deal-breaker until resolved:** the sister's possible non-consent to the 2004 partition (if she did not sign, she may still have a share). Advocate needed.
- **Major:** the 2018 mortgage without a registered release. Bank closure and release needed before sale.
- **Minor:** water-logging on the north side; reflect in price and design.
- **Refuse:** the cash token; ₹5 lakh in cash breaks the cash limit. Token by bank transfer only, after the advocate's first review.
Decision: "Proceed only with conditions": the advocate checks the partition; the seller clears the mortgage; token by bank transfer with a written receipt that refers to these conditions.

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** always, for the title opinion on any sale.
- **Licensed surveyor:** whenever area or boundaries are unclear.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Housing.com (April 2025): how to get an encumbrance certificate in Kerala](https://housing.com/news/steps-to-get-an-encumbrance-certificate-in-kerala/amp) | Re-check the EC process for your checklist | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Kerala State Disaster Management Authority: hazard maps (flood, landslide)](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/hazard-maps/) | Re-check hazard maps for the property | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [eCourts Services (eCommittee, Supreme Court of India): case status by party name, CNR number, court orders, caveats](https://services.ecourts.gov.in/) | Party-name search for litigation | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Choose a real property where the owner gives written permission (best: your family's), or use the sample case above.
2. Run the full checklist, recording evidence for each item.
3. Classify every issue as minor, major or deal-breaker, and name the professional for each.
4. Write a one-page due-diligence summary for the client, with a clear decision and conditions.

**Proof to record:** The completed checklist with evidence (private), the issue classification and the one-page summary.

## Template: Due-diligence checklist

```
DUE-DILIGENCE CHECKLIST (one per property; tick and attach proof)
OWNERSHIP AND TITLE                                          Done  Proof file
[ ] Copy of the current title deed (aadharam) seen and read     __    ______
[ ] Prior deeds (title chain) for at least 30 years, if possible __   ______
[ ] Encumbrance certificate (EC) for 30+ years (mortgages, sales, attachments) __ ______
[ ] Seller's name matches deed, EC, thandaper, land tax receipt and ID __ ______
[ ] All co-owners / legal heirs identified and willing to sign  __    ______
[ ] Power of attorney (if any): original, registered, still valid, principal alive __ ______
[ ] Possession certificate / location certificate from the village office __ ______
[ ] Latest land tax (karam) receipt                             __    ______
[ ] Mutation (pokkuvaravu) done in the seller's name            __    ______
LAND RECORDS AND SURVEY
[ ] Survey / resurvey number and sub-division match all papers  __    ______
[ ] Sketch / FMB from the village or e-Rekha; area matches the deed __ ______
[ ] Land type in revenue records (purayidam / nilam / thottam / data bank) __ ______
[ ] Not in the paddy/wetland data bank (or conversion order exists) __ ______
[ ] Not government, puramboke, forest or excess (surplus) land  __    ______
BUILDING (if any)
[ ] Building permit and approved plan from the panchayat/municipality __ ______
[ ] Occupancy certificate / building number; building tax receipt __ ______
[ ] Built area matches the permit (no unauthorised additions)   __    ______
LOCATION AND RISK
[ ] Physical visit: boundaries match sketch; neighbours confirm __    ______
[ ] Access road: public road or registered right of way; width __    ______
[ ] Flood, landslide and water-logging check (KSDMA maps, neighbours, 2018/2019 floods) __ ______
[ ] CRZ (coastal), ESA (Western Ghats), forest buffer, quarry nearby __ ______
[ ] Land-use / master plan zoning (municipalities) if known      __    ______
[ ] Electricity, water, drainage, mobile signal                  __    ______
DISPUTES AND DEBTS
[ ] No pending case (ask seller in writing; advocate searches)  __    ______
[ ] No bank loan or attachment on EC; loan closure letter if there was one __ ______
[ ] No tenant or occupant claim; no encroachment                __    ______
PROFESSIONAL SIGN-OFF
[ ] Advocate's title opinion (written)                          __    ______
[ ] Licensed surveyor's measurement (if boundaries or area are unclear) __ ______
DECISION: proceed / proceed with conditions / walk away   Reason: ______
```

## Template: Due-diligence summary

```
DUE-DILIGENCE SUMMARY        Property ______  For client ______  Date ______
Prepared by ______ (broker; this is not a legal opinion)
Checks completed: title chain __ EC __ land records __ land type __ building __ site __ litigation __
DEAL-BREAKERS: ______
MAJOR (advocate / surveyor needed): ______
MINOR (seller to fix): ______
RECOMMENDATION: proceed / proceed with conditions / do not proceed
Conditions: ______
Next step: advocate's written title opinion by ______ ; token only by bank transfer with conditions
```

## Common mistakes

- **Telling a client the title is clear.** Only an advocate gives a title opinion.
- **Skipping evidence.** Record a file or photo for every item.
- **Letting a client pay a big token before checks.** Keep the token small and conditional.

## Local fraud warning

**Pressure to skip checks.** "Another buyer is ready; pay today" is a classic pressure tactic. A genuine seller with clean papers can wait a few days for an advocate's check.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Who gives the title opinion?
    - A) An advocate
    - B) The broker
    - C) The neighbour
    - D) The seller
2. In the sample case, what is the biggest issue?
    - A) Water-logging
    - B) The road width
    - C) The price per cent
    - D) A sibling who may not have agreed to the partition
3. When should a licensed surveyor be called?
    - A) Only for flats
    - B) Never
    - C) Only after registration
    - D) When area or boundaries are unclear or disputed
4. How should the token be paid in the sample case?
    - A) By bank transfer with a written receipt and conditions
    - B) In gold
    - C) In cash
    - D) By a promise

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the full checklist
- **Action:** run the full due-diligence checklist on a real (permitted) property or the sample case. It is done when your proof is saved: the completed checklist with evidence (private), the issue classification and the one-page summary.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Your checklist supports the advocate's work.
2. **D.** She may still have a share.
3. **D.** Surveyors measure and fix boundaries.
4. **A.** Cash limits and safety.

sections.title: Module 7: Valuation
sections.summary: Valuation: fair value and market value, the comparables method with adjustments, the income and cost methods, the value drivers in Kerala, and a local market study of 20+ real listings with fair value comparisons.
sections.content:
*Part B: Knowledge base.*

## Overview

Valuation is how you stay honest with owners ("your price is 20% above comparable sales") and protect buyers. You will not give formal valuations (banks use their own licensed valuers); you will give clients evidence-based price ranges. Rates and rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Explain fair value, market value and bank valuation.
- Value land and houses by comparables with adjustments.
- Use the income and cost methods.
- Run a local market study with 20+ listings.

## Time

About 4 hours 45 minutes in total: 3 hours 45 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: week 6, with the module project due in week 6.

## Lessons

1. RE-M07-L01: Fair value, market value and comparables (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M07-L02: Income and cost methods, and what raises or lowers value (about 1 hour)
3. RE-M07-L03: Your local market study (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- Comparables sheet and adjustment table (RE-M07-L01).
- Income and cost valuation sheet (RE-M07-L02).
- Market study summary (RE-M07-L03).

## Module project: a local market study report

1. Complete the Comps sheet (20+ listings) and fair value comparison.
2. Value one subject property by comparables and one other method.
3. Write a 1 to 2 page market report for Kuttiady (or your area): medians by locality, drivers, discount, risks.
4. Share it with one broker you interviewed and note their feedback.

**Proof to record:** The Comps sheet, the valuation and the report with the broker's feedback.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Comps tab with formulas and 20+ listings.
- Valuation sheet (income and cost).
- Market study report.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data | Under 10 listings | 10 to 19 listings | 20+ listings with sources and dates |
| Method | Asking prices only | Comparables without adjustments | Adjusted comparables plus a second method |
| Fair value | Not checked | 1 to 4 checked | 5+ checked with gap calculated |
| Report | No report | Numbers only | Clear medians, drivers, discount and risks |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Collect 10 listings and calculate price per cent.
- Check fair value for 2 of them.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Fair value | Government minimum value for stamp duty. |
| Market value | What a willing, informed buyer pays a willing seller. |
| Comparables method | Value from adjusted recent similar sales and listings. |
| Median | Middle value; less affected by extremes. |
| NOI | Rent after vacancy minus operating costs, before loans. |
| Cap rate | NOI ÷ value. |
| Cost method | Land + building cost new − depreciation. |
| Strongest Kerala value drivers | Road, distance, land type, title. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Calling yourself a valuer.** Banks use licensed valuers; you give evidence-based ranges.
- **Ignoring risks in value.** Flood, title and land type reduce value.
- **Not updating your sheet.** Add 3 listings each week.

sections.title: RE-M07-L01: Fair value, market value and comparables
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can explain fair value versus market value, build a comparables sheet with price per cent and per sq ft, and adjust comparables to estimate a fair range. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes on comparables).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

All prices in this module's examples are **illustrative numbers for practice**, not real market data or recommendations. Your own comparables sheet gives you the real local numbers.

**Fair value vs market value.**
- **Fair value** is the government's notified minimum value per are for each survey number, used for stamp duty (RE-M03-L03, RE-M04-L01). It was raised by 20% from 1 April 2023 ([Onmanorama](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2023/03/28/kerala-increases-land-fair-value.html); check current rules). It is usually **below** the market price in Kerala and changes only when the government revises it.
- **Market value** is the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller, both well informed and under no pressure. Asking prices are **not** market value: they are what sellers hope for. Actual sale prices are better, but are hard to find (deeds sometimes show the fair value rather than the real price).
- A bank's **valuation** for a loan is a third figure, made by its empanelled valuer.

**The comparables method (sales comparison).** The main way to value land and houses:
1. Collect recent **comparable** listings and, wherever possible, actual sale prices (ask brokers and document writers) in the same area.
2. Calculate **price per cent** for land and **price per sq ft** for buildings (state the area basis).
3. **Adjust** each comparable for differences from the subject property: road, distance, size, shape, flood risk, title.
4. Use the **median** of the adjusted prices (less affected by extremes than the average) and give a **range**, not a single number.

**Value drivers in Kerala:**
| Driver | Effect | Strength |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Road frontage and width | Plots on a wide tarred road sell far higher than plots on a narrow path | Strong |
| Distance to town, bus stand, school, hospital | Closer is usually higher | Strong |
| Title quality | Clean, simple title sells faster and higher; doubtful title sells at a big discount | Strong |
| Land type | Purayidam vs nilam or data bank land; nilam can be worth a fraction | Very strong |
| Shape and level | Regular, level plots are easier to build on | Medium |
| Flood and slope risk | Flood-prone or steep land is discounted, more so since 2018 | Medium to strong |
| Size | Small plots (5 to 10 cents) often have a higher price per cent than large ones | Medium |
| Surroundings | Quarries, power lines and garbage sites reduce value; good neighbours and views add | Medium |
| Water and utilities | A good well and KWA water add value | Medium |
| Infrastructure plans | New roads, bypasses, rail or institutions can raise prices; also risk of acquisition | Variable |

**Asking vs selling.** In many Kozhikode localities, final prices may settle below asking prices, and some listings never sell. Ask local brokers what discount is typical and note it in your sheet.

The comparables sheet with working formulas is in the templates below and in your toolkit.

## Local example

A 10-cent plot (subject) on a 4 m panchayat road, 2 km from Kuttiady town. Four comparables:

| Comp | Details | Asking per cent | Adjustment | Adjusted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 8 cents, same road, 1.8 km | ₹2,40,000 | −5% (smaller plot, closer) | ₹2,28,000 |
| B | 12 cents, 6 m road, 1.5 km | ₹2,80,000 | −15% (better road, closer) | ₹2,38,000 |
| C | 15 cents, narrow path, 3 km | ₹1,60,000 | +20% (worse road, farther) | ₹1,92,000 |
| D | 10 cents, same road, 2.2 km, sold last month | ₹2,10,000 (sold) | 0% | ₹2,10,000 |

Median of adjusted values: (₹2,10,000 + ₹2,28,000) ÷ 2 = **₹2,19,000** per cent. Range about ₹2.0 to ₹2.35 lakh per cent, so the 10-cent plot is roughly ₹20 to ₹23.5 lakh. Comparable D (an actual sale) deserves extra weight. The adjustment percentages are judgement: learn them from local brokers and actual sales.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Housing.com: how to check the fair value of land in Kerala](https://housing.com/news/how-to-check-the-fair-value-of-land-in-kerala) | Re-read how to search fair value | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [MagicBricks (property portal)](https://www.magicbricks.com/) | Search land and house listings for Kozhikode district | 15 minutes | unverified: the site blocks automated checks; type the address yourself |
| [99acres (property portal)](https://www.99acres.com/) | Search the same, to compare portals | 10 minutes | found in a web search 2026-11-04; page not opened, so unverified |
| [Housing.com (property portal)](https://housing.com/) | Search the same | 10 minutes | found in a web search 2026-11-04; page not opened, so unverified |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Create the Comps tab in your workbook with the header row and formulas.
2. Add your first 10 real listings (land and houses) around Kuttiady and Kozhikode from portals, local brokers, newspaper adverts and WhatsApp groups (record the source; don't copy personal phone numbers you weren't given).
3. Choose one subject plot and adjust 3 to 4 comparables for it, as in the example.
4. Ask one broker what discount from asking price is typical in your area.

**Proof to record:** The Comps sheet with 10 rows and working formulas, one adjustment table and the broker's answer.

## Template: Comparables sheet

```
Date seen,Source (portal/broker/owner),Link or contact,Locality,Panchayat/municipality,Type (land/house/flat/commercial),Land area (cents),Built-up area (sq ft),Asking price (Rs),Price per cent (Rs),Price per sq ft (Rs),Road frontage (ft),Road width (ft),Distance to town (km),Flood/slope notes,Status (asking/sold/withdrawn),Notes

COMPARABLES SHEET (tab "Comps")  Row 1 = headers above. In row 2:
J2 (price per cent):   =IF(G2>0, I2/G2, "")
K2 (price per sq ft):  =IF(H2>0, I2/H2, "")
Copy J2:K2 down. Summary cells (land only, for one locality):
Median price per cent: =MEDIAN(FILTER(J2:J200, F2:F200="land", D2:D200="Kuttiady"))
Count of land listings: =COUNTIFS(F2:F200,"land",D2:D200,"Kuttiady")
(LibreOffice without FILTER: use a pivot table, or sort and pick the middle value.)
Rule: compare like with like (same area, similar size, similar road access).
```

## Template: Comparable adjustment table

```
COMPARABLE ADJUSTMENT    Subject: ______ cents, road ___ m, ___ km to town
Comp | Source | Size | Road | Distance | Other | Price/cent | Adj % | Adjusted
A    |        |      |      |          |       |            |       | =G2*(1+H2)
B ...
Median adjusted: =MEDIAN(I2:I6)   Range: low ______ high ______
Weight actual sales more than asking prices. Typical asking-to-sale discount here: ___%
```

## Common mistakes

- **Treating asking prices as market value.** Find actual sales and note the usual discount.
- **Comparing unlike properties.** Adjust for road, distance, size and risk.
- **Giving one exact number.** Give a range and explain it.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake comparables.** Some sellers and brokers quote "the plot next door sold for ₹3 lakh per cent" to push prices. Ask for proof (a deed copy or a broker who handled it) or treat it as a claim only.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is fair value in Kerala?
    - A) The bank's valuation
    - B) The market price
    - C) The government's notified minimum value for stamp duty
    - D) The asking price
2. Why use the median of adjusted comparables?
    - A) It is easier to type
    - B) It is always higher
    - C) It is less affected by extreme values
    - D) It is the law
3. A comparable has a much better road than the subject. How do you adjust it?
    - A) Adjust it up
    - B) No adjustment
    - C) Remove all comparables
    - D) Adjust its price down to compare with the subject
4. Which is better evidence of market value?
    - A) A WhatsApp forward
    - B) An asking price on a portal
    - C) The seller's hope
    - D) A recent actual sale price

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the value drivers table
- **Action:** build your Comps sheet with 10 real listings and adjust comparables for one plot. It is done when your proof is saved: the Comps sheet with 10 rows and working formulas, one adjustment table and the broker's answer.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** It usually lags the market.
2. **C.** One odd listing can distort an average.
3. **D.** The subject is worse on that driver.
4. **D.** Actual sales show what buyers paid.
