sections.title: RE-M07-L02: Income and cost methods, and what raises or lowers value
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can value a rented property by the income method (cap rate) and a house by the cost method, and cross-check them with comparables. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 35 minutes on calculations).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

All prices in this module's examples are **illustrative numbers for practice**, not real market data or recommendations. Your own comparables sheet gives you the real local numbers.

**Income method (capitalisation).** For property bought for rent (shops, offices, rental houses):
- **Net operating income (NOI)** = annual rent after vacancy, minus property and land tax, maintenance, insurance and management (not loan payments).
- **Capitalisation rate (cap rate)** = NOI ÷ value. If similar properties sell at a cap rate of, say, 4%, then **value = NOI ÷ 0.04**.
- Residential rental yields in Kerala are often low compared with interest rates (many investors earn more from price growth than from rent; check local numbers in your own ROI sheet, RE-M08-L02).

**Cost method.** Value = **land value** (from comparables) + **cost to build the building today** − **depreciation** (age, wear, outdated design).
- Construction cost per sq ft depends on quality and changes with material and labour costs (RE-M17). Ask two local contractors or engineers for current rates.
- Depreciation: a simple method is straight-line over the building's useful life (for example 60 years for a concrete house); older, poorly maintained houses lose more.
- Useful for **new or unique houses** where few comparables exist, and to check that a house price is not far above what it would cost to build.

**Cross-checking.** A good valuation uses two or three methods. If the comparables say ₹48 lakh, the cost method says ₹52 lakh and the income method says ₹30 lakh, the house is priced as a home to live in, not as an investment.

Further study: the [MIT OCW real estate finance course](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/11-431j-real-estate-finance-and-investment-fall-2006) explains valuation and cap rates in depth (advanced; read the lecture notes on valuation when you are ready). The [Personal Finance lesson on gold, REITs and real estate](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m09-l06) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course) covers real estate inside a personal portfolio.

## Local example

**A shop room in Kuttiady town** rents for ₹18,000 a month.
- Gross rent: 18,000 × 12 = ₹2,16,000
- Vacancy 1 month: −₹18,000; building tax and maintenance: −₹20,000
- NOI: 2,16,000 − 18,000 − 20,000 = **₹1,78,000**
- If similar shops sell at a 5% cap rate: value = 1,78,000 ÷ 0.05 = **₹35.6 lakh**
- At a 6% cap rate: 1,78,000 ÷ 0.06 = **₹29.7 lakh**. A one-point change in cap rate changes the value by about ₹6 lakh.

**A 5-year-old house on 8 cents** near Kakkattil, 1,400 sq ft:
- Land: 8 × ₹2,20,000 = ₹17,60,000 (from comparables)
- Building cost new (illustrative ₹2,200 per sq ft): 1,400 × 2,200 = ₹30,80,000
- Depreciation over 60 years, 5 years used: 30,80,000 × 5 ÷ 60 = ₹2,56,667
- Cost-method value: 17,60,000 + 30,80,000 − 2,56,667 ≈ **₹45.8 lakh**
If it is listed at ₹62 lakh, either comparables support a premium (location, finish) or it is overpriced.

## Worked calculation

**In Google Sheets or LibreOffice:**
- NOI: `=B1*(12-B2)-B3-B4` (B1 monthly rent, B2 vacancy months, B3 taxes, B4 maintenance)
- Value at cap rate: `=NOI/B5` (B5 cap rate such as 0.05)
- Cost method: `=land + build_cost_new - build_cost_new*age/useful_life`
- Sensitivity: put cap rates 0.04, 0.05, 0.06, 0.07 in a column and `=$NOI/A2` beside each.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare 11.431J Real Estate Finance and Investment (Geltner and McGrath, CC BY-NC-SA)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/11-431j-real-estate-finance-and-investment-fall-2006) | Open the course and skim the lecture notes list for valuation topics (advanced, optional) | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Principles of Finance (OpenStax) on LibreTexts: chapter list including time value of money (chapters 7-9)](https://biz.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Finance/Principles_of_Finance_%28OpenStax%29) | Look at the chapter list; time value of money chapters support income valuation | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Find one rented property locally (shop or house) where the owner or broker will tell you the rent.
2. Value it by the income method at three cap rates.
3. Find one house listing and value it by the cost method, using land comparables and a construction cost from a local contractor.
4. Compare both results with the asking prices and write what you conclude.

**Proof to record:** Two calculations with sources for each input, and your conclusion.

## Template: Income and cost valuation sheet

```
INCOME METHOD               COST METHOD
B1 Monthly rent             C1 Land cents
B2 Vacancy months           C2 Land price per cent (comps)
B3 Taxes per year           C3 Land value         =C1*C2
B4 Maintenance per year     C4 Built-up sq ft
B5 Other costs              C5 Build cost per sq ft (2 contractor quotes)
B6 NOI =B1*(12-B2)-B3-B4-B5 C6 Cost new           =C4*C5
B7 Cap rate                 C7 Age (years)  C8 Useful life (years)
B8 Value =B6/B7             C9 Depreciation       =C6*C7/C8
                            C10 Value             =C3+C6-C9
Comparables value: ______   Asking price: ______   Conclusion: ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Including loan EMIs in NOI.** NOI is before financing.
- **Using a builder's marketing cost per sq ft.** Get quotes from local contractors.
- **Relying on one method.** Cross-check with comparables.

## Local fraud warning

**Inflated rent claims.** Sellers of "investment" shops or houses sometimes show inflated rent (a relative as tenant, a short-term agreement) to raise the value. Ask for the rental agreement, bank statements of rent received and the tenant's history.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Value by the income method equals:
    - A) Price per cent × cents
    - B) Rent × 100
    - C) NOI ÷ cap rate
    - D) EMI × 12
2. What is NOI?
    - A) Rent minus EMI
    - B) Annual rent after vacancy minus operating costs, before loan payments
    - C) The asking price
    - D) Monthly rent
3. When is the cost method most useful?
    - A) For new or unique houses with few comparables
    - B) For empty land only
    - C) Never
    - D) For shares
4. If NOI is ₹1,20,000 and the cap rate is 4%, what is the value?
    - A) ₹30 lakh
    - B) ₹1.2 crore
    - C) ₹3 lakh
    - D) ₹4.8 lakh

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and both worked examples
- **Action:** value one rented property by the income method and one house by the cost method. It is done when your proof is saved: two calculations with sources for each input, and your conclusion.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Lower cap rates mean higher values.
2. **B.** Financing is separate.
3. **A.** It shows the replacement cost.
4. **A.** 1,20,000 ÷ 0.04.

sections.title: RE-M07-L03: Your local market study
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can complete a local market study with 20+ real listings, compare government fair values with market prices, and summarise prices by locality. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (10 minutes reading, 60 minutes of market work (spread over the week)).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

All prices in this module's examples are **illustrative numbers for practice**, not real market data or recommendations. Your own comparables sheet gives you the real local numbers.

This is one of the course's key practical tasks: a **local market study** of Kuttiady and Kozhikode with **at least 20 real listings** (land and houses), plus the **government fair value** for several of them.

**Where to find listings:**
- Free portals: MagicBricks, 99acres, Housing.com, NoBroker (filter by Kozhikode, locality and property type).
- OLX and Facebook Marketplace (verify carefully; many are outdated).
- Local brokers and their WhatsApp status updates; newspaper classifieds (Mathrubhumi and Malayala Manorama classifieds).
- Boards on plots ("land for sale" with a phone number).
Record the source and date for each. Never collect or share personal data you have not been given for this purpose.

**What to record:** follow the comps header (date, source, locality, type, land area, built-up area, asking price, road, distance, flood or slope notes, status).

**Fair value comparison:** for at least 5 listings where you know the village and survey number (or a nearby one), look up the fair value on the official portal and calculate:
- Fair value per cent = fair value per are ÷ 2.471
- **Gap** = (asking per cent − fair value per cent) ÷ fair value per cent

**Summary by locality:** median price per cent for land and median price per sq ft for houses, with the count of listings. Note what drives the differences (road, distance, town).

**Use it every week:** add 3 new listings in your weekly log (re-system track) so your sheet stays current.

## Local example

Sachin's sheet after two weeks (illustrative figures):

| Locality | Land listings | Median per cent | Houses | Median per sq ft (incl. land) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kuttiady town (within 1 km) | 4 | ₹4.5 lakh | 2 | ₹4,800 |
| Kuttiady (2 to 5 km) | 6 | ₹2.1 lakh | 3 | ₹3,600 |
| Kayakkody / Velom | 4 | ₹1.6 lakh | 1 | ₹3,100 |
| Kozhikode city (Mavoor Road area) | 3 | ₹18 lakh | 2 | ₹7,500 |

Fair value check for five listings: fair values were 25% to 45% of asking prices. A seller who says "fair value is ₹70,000 per cent, so ₹1.6 lakh is cheap" is mixing two different things.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [MagicBricks (property portal)](https://www.magicbricks.com/) | Search Kozhikode listings | 15 minutes | unverified: the site blocks automated checks; type the address yourself |
| [99acres (property portal)](https://www.99acres.com/) | Search Kozhikode listings | 15 minutes | found in a web search 2026-11-04; page not opened, so unverified |
| [Housing.com (property portal)](https://housing.com/) | Search Kozhikode listings | 15 minutes | found in a web search 2026-11-04; page not opened, so unverified |
| [NoBroker: list your property for rent or sale (free for owners)](https://www.nobroker.in/list-your-property-for-rent-sale) | Search owner listings | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Housing.com: how to check the fair value of land in Kerala](https://housing.com/news/how-to-check-the-fair-value-of-land-in-kerala) | Fair value search steps | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Bring your Comps sheet to at least 20 real listings (land and houses) around Kuttiady and Kozhikode, with sources and dates.
2. Look up fair values for at least 5 of them on the official portal and calculate the gap.
3. Make a summary table by locality (median per cent, median per sq ft, counts).
4. Write a half-page market note: what drives prices here, what surprised you and the typical asking-to-sale discount you were told.

**Proof to record:** The Comps sheet with 20+ rows, the fair value comparison for 5 listings, the summary table and your market note.

**Full-time track:** Aim for 40 listings and visit 5 localities in person.

## Template: Market study summary

```
MARKET STUDY SUMMARY      Area ______  Period ______  Listings ___ (target 20+)
Locality | Land count | Median ₹/cent =MEDIAN(FILTER(Comps!J:J,Comps!D:D=A2,Comps!F:F="land")) | House count | Median ₹/sq ft
FAIR VALUE CHECK
Listing | Village | Survey | Fair value per are | per cent (=x/2.471) | Asking per cent | Gap % (=(asking-fv)/fv)
NOTES: price drivers ______ ; typical discount from asking ___% ; sources used ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Counting duplicates.** The same plot often appears on several portals; list it once.
- **Using old listings.** Record dates and remove stale ones.
- **Mixing land and house prices per sq ft.** Keep land per cent and house per sq ft separate.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake listings to collect leads.** Some portal ads show attractive "properties" that don't exist, to collect buyer numbers. If the details are vague and the poster won't share the location, treat it as unreliable.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How many listings should your market study include?
    - A) At least 20
    - B) 2
    - C) 1,000
    - D) 5
2. How do you convert a fair value per are to per cent?
    - A) Multiply by 100
    - B) Divide by 2.471
    - C) Divide by 435.6
    - D) Multiply by 40.47
3. Why record the date of each listing?
    - A) For tax
    - B) So you can remove stale listings and see trends
    - C) It is not needed
    - D) For the seller
4. A seller says "fair value is low, so my price is cheap." What is wrong?
    - A) Fair value is a duty minimum, not a measure of market price
    - B) Nothing
    - C) Fair value is always higher
    - D) Fair value is always the market price

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and plan your sources
- **Action:** complete a market study with 20+ listings and fair value comparisons. It is done when your proof is saved: the Comps sheet with 20+ rows, the fair value comparison for 5 listings, the summary table and your market note.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Enough to see a pattern.
2. **B.** 1 are = 2.471 cents.
3. **B.** Markets change.
4. **A.** Compare with comparables instead.

sections.title: Module 8: Real estate finance
sections.summary: Real estate finance: home loans and loans against property, eligibility, EMIs, leverage risk, the full cost of buying and owning, rental yield, cap rate, cash-on-cash return and basic IRR, with honest numbers on why small investors often earn less than they expect.
sections.content:
*Part B: Knowledge base.*

## Overview

These numbers let you advise clients honestly and, later, judge your own investments. Interest rates and bank rules change: rates here are illustrations; get current ones from banks. Rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Estimate loan eligibility, down payment and EMI.
- Calculate the full cost of buying and owning.
- Calculate yields, cash-on-cash and IRR.
- Explain leverage and the honest risks of property investing.

## Time

About 3 hours 45 minutes in total: 2 hours 45 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: week 7, with the module project due in week 7.

## Lessons

1. RE-M08-L01: Home loans, loans against property, eligibility and EMIs (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M08-L02: Rental yield, cap rate, cash-on-cash, IRR and the total cost of owning (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- EMI formulas and loan eligibility calculator (RE-M08-L01).
- Full cost of a purchase (RE-M08-L02).
- Rental yield and return calculator (RE-M08-L02).

## Module project: an affordability and return pack: one buyer and 5 properties

1. Work out eligibility, down payment and own money needed for one buyer (sample or real with permission).
2. Complete the Cost tab for one purchase with current official rates.
3. Complete the ROI tab for 5 real properties.
4. Write one page comparing the results with a fixed deposit and an index fund (from the Personal Finance course).

**Proof to record:** The Loan, Cost and ROI tabs and the one-page comparison.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Loan tab (eligibility and EMI).
- Cost tab (full purchase cost).
- ROI tab with 5 properties.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Loans | No calculation | EMI only | Eligibility, LTV, down payment and own money |
| Costs | Price only | Some costs | All buying and owning costs with dated rates |
| Returns | Gross yield only | Net yield | Net yield, cash-on-cash and IRR for 5 properties |
| Honesty | Promises returns | Mentions risk | Compares with alternatives and states risks plainly |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Calculate one EMI and one gross yield.
- Fill in the Cost tab for one purchase.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| LTV up to ₹30 lakh | 90% (RBI). |
| EMI formula | =-PMT(rate/12, years*12, loan). |
| LAP | Loan against property you own; risk of losing it. |
| Gross yield | Annual rent ÷ price. |
| Net yield / cap rate | NOI ÷ price. |
| Cash-on-cash | Cash flow after EMI ÷ own cash. |
| IRR | Yearly return including all cash flows and the sale. |
| Kerala buying costs | About 10% to 12% of price. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Ignoring interest costs.** Total interest can exceed the loan.
- **Recommending investments.** Teach clients to evaluate; don't recommend.
- **Using old rates.** Date-stamp rates and check banks.

sections.title: RE-M08-L01: Home loans, loans against property, eligibility and EMIs
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can explain home loans and loans against property, estimate a buyer's loan eligibility and down payment, and calculate EMIs in Sheets. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes on calculations and a bank visit).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Interest rates, fees and bank rules change and differ by bank. The 8.5% rate used here is an **illustration only**; get current rates from banks. This is education, not financial advice. Rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Home loan.** A loan to buy or build a house, or to buy a plot and build on it. Banks, housing finance companies and cooperative banks lend. Key terms:
- **Loan-to-value (LTV):** the maximum share of the property value the bank can lend. RBI limits for housing loans (as reported in 2015, [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/pf/home-buyers-can-now-get-more-loan-for-property-up-to-rs-30-lakh-115100801016_1.html); check current rules):
| Loan amount | Maximum LTV |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹30 lakh | Up to 90% of the property value |
| Above ₹30 lakh up to ₹75 lakh | Up to 80% |
| Above ₹75 lakh | Up to 75% |
  Stamp duty and registration costs are usually **not** included in the value for LTV, so the buyer pays them from savings.
- **Eligibility:** banks look at income, existing EMIs, age, job stability, credit score and the property's legal and technical check. Many banks keep total EMIs within roughly 40% to 60% of net monthly income (this ratio varies by bank and is not a fixed rule).
- **Interest:** floating rates linked to a benchmark are common; the rate changes over the loan's life.
- **Fees:** processing fee, legal and valuation charges, and mortgage registration costs.
- **Process:** application → documents → sanction letter → bank's legal check (title, 13 to 30 year EC) and technical valuation → agreement → registration of the sale deed and mortgage → disbursement to the seller.
- **Plot loans** (for land only) usually have lower LTV and stricter rules; agricultural or nilam land generally won't qualify.

**Loan against property (LAP).** A loan secured on property you already own, used for business or other needs. Interest is usually higher than home loans, and you can **lose the property** if you can't repay.

**EMI.** Equated monthly instalment. In Sheets or LibreOffice:
```
EMI FORMULAS
Monthly EMI:      =-PMT(annual_rate/12, years*12, loan_amount)
Example:          =-PMT(0.085/12, 20*12, 2500000)   -> about Rs 21,700
Total paid:       =EMI*years*12
Total interest:   =EMI*years*12 - loan_amount
Max loan from an EMI you can afford: =-PV(annual_rate/12, years*12, EMI)
```

**Leverage risk.** A loan lets you control a bigger property, but EMIs are fixed while rents and prices are not. If the tenant leaves, rates rise or prices fall, the borrower still pays. Many families in Kerala have been stretched by loans for houses built bigger than their income could support. The [Personal Finance lesson on home and other loans](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m06-l03) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course) and [rent-or-buy lesson](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m11-l02) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course) go deeper.

## Local example

**A teacher couple** with a combined net income of ₹45,000 a month and an existing vehicle EMI of ₹5,000 want a house worth ₹25 lakh near Kuttiady.
- If the bank allows total EMIs of 50% of net income: 45,000 × 0.5 = ₹22,500; minus ₹5,000 existing = **₹17,500** for the new EMI.
- Maximum loan at 8.5% for 20 years: `=-PV(0.085/12, 240, 17500)` ≈ **₹20.2 lakh**.
- LTV limit: ₹25 lakh is below ₹30 lakh, so up to 90% = ₹22.5 lakh. Income is the tighter limit: about **₹20.2 lakh**.
- Down payment: 25 − 20.2 = **₹4.8 lakh**, plus stamp duty and fee (about ₹2.5 lakh at 10%) and other costs: they need about **₹7.5 lakh** of their own money.
Sachin tells them this before showing houses, so they don't fall in love with a house they can't afford.

## Worked calculation

- EMI on ₹20 lakh at 8.5% for 20 years: `=-PMT(0.085/12, 240, 2000000)` ≈ **₹17,357**
- Total paid: 17,357 × 240 ≈ ₹41.7 lakh; total interest ≈ **₹21.7 lakh**, more than the loan itself.
- Same loan for 15 years: `=-PMT(0.085/12, 180, 2000000)` ≈ ₹19,695; total interest ≈ ₹15.5 lakh.
- If the rate rises to 10% (20 years): ≈ ₹19,300 a month, about ₹1,950 more.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RBI LTV limits for housing loans | Up to ₹30 lakh: 90%; ₹30–75 lakh: 80%; above ₹75 lakh: 75% | Business Standard, October 2015 |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Bank's advocate and valuer:** do the legal and technical checks for the loan.
- **Chartered accountant:** tax benefits on home loans, which depend on the tax regime and current law.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Business Standard (8 October 2015): RBI loan-to-value limits for home loans](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/pf/home-buyers-can-now-get-more-loan-for-property-up-to-rs-30-lakh-115100801016_1.html) | Read the LTV rules | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Principles of Finance (OpenStax) on LibreTexts: chapter list including time value of money (chapters 7-9)](https://biz.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Finance/Principles_of_Finance_%28OpenStax%29) | Read the time value of money chapter on loans and annuities (chapters 7 to 9) | 30 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [OpenStax, Principles of Finance (free, CC BY-NC-SA)](https://openstax.org/books/principles-finance/pages/preface) | Use the OpenStax book as the reference for the formulas | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Add the EMI formulas to your workbook and check that ₹25 lakh at 8.5% for 20 years gives about ₹21,700.
2. Visit or call one bank and one cooperative bank near you and ask: current home loan rate range, processing fee, documents needed, how long sanction takes, and whether they finance plots. Note the date.
3. Work out the eligibility and down payment for a sample buyer (or a real client with permission).
4. Write a one-page "home loan basics" sheet for your clients.

**Proof to record:** Your EMI sheet, notes from two lenders with dates, one eligibility calculation and your client sheet.

## Template: Loan eligibility calculator

```
LOAN ELIGIBILITY (tab "Loan")    rates as of ______ (ask the bank)
B1 Net monthly income            B2 Existing EMIs
B3 EMI ratio allowed (e.g. 0.5)  B4 Max new EMI          =B1*B3-B2
B5 Interest rate (e.g. 0.085)    B6 Years (e.g. 20)
B7 Max loan by income            =-PV(B5/12, B6*12, B4)
B8 Property value                B9 LTV limit            =IF(B8<=3000000,0.9,IF(B8<=7500000,0.8,0.75))
B10 Max loan by LTV              =B8*B9
B11 Loan possible                =MIN(B7,B10)
B12 Down payment                 =B8-B11
B13 Stamp duty + fee (10%)       =MAX(B8,fair_value)*0.10
B14 Own money needed             =B12+B13+other_costs
```

## Common mistakes

- **Showing houses before checking affordability.** Work out eligibility first.
- **Forgetting that stamp duty is not financed.** Plan for it in own money.
- **Assuming rates stay fixed.** Test a higher rate.

## Local fraud warning

**Loan "agents" promising guaranteed sanction.** Some take fees to "arrange" loans on property with title problems or fake income papers. Fake income documents are fraud. Send clients directly to banks and never touch fake papers.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is the maximum LTV for a ₹25 lakh home loan under the RBI limits?
    - A) 75%
    - B) 50%
    - C) 90%
    - D) 100%
2. Which formula gives the monthly EMI in Sheets?
    - A) =loan/12
    - B) =-PMT(rate/12, years*12, loan)
    - C) =PV(loan)
    - D) =SUM(loan)
3. Why is a loan against property risky?
    - A) It has no interest
    - B) It is illegal
    - C) It can't be repaid early
    - D) You can lose the property if you can't repay
4. What costs does a buyer usually pay from own money?
    - A) Nothing
    - B) Down payment plus stamp duty and registration
    - C) Only the EMI
    - D) Only the broker

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the EMI formulas
- **Action:** build the EMI and eligibility sheets and collect loan terms from two lenders. It is done when your proof is saved: your EMI sheet, notes from two lenders with dates, one eligibility calculation and your client sheet.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Up to ₹30 lakh: 90%.
2. **B.** PMT gives the payment.
3. **D.** The property is security.
4. **B.** Banks lend on property value, not duty.

sections.title: RE-M08-L02: Rental yield, cap rate, cash-on-cash, IRR and the total cost of owning
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can calculate the full cost of buying and owning a property, gross and net rental yield, cap rate, cash-on-cash return and a basic IRR, and explain why many small investors earn less than they expect. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes reading, 70 minutes on calculations for 5 real properties).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Interest rates, fees and bank rules change and differ by bank. The 8.5% rate used here is an **illustration only**; get current rates from banks. This is education, not financial advice. Rules are as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Total cost of buying** (cost tab in your toolkit; RE-M04-L01):
- Price + stamp duty (8%) + registration fee (2%) on the higher of price or fair value, + document writer or advocate fee + EC and copies + brokerage (often 1% to 2%, plus 18% GST if the broker is registered) + loan fees.
- In Kerala, buying costs often add **10% to 12%** to the price, so a property must rise that much just to break even.
- TDS (1% if the value is ₹50 lakh or more) is not an extra cost: it is part of the price paid to the government on the seller's behalf (RE-M09-L01).

**Cost of owning:** land tax, building tax, maintenance, repairs, insurance, electricity and water when vacant, caretaking if you live away, and the **opportunity cost** (what the money could earn elsewhere, for example in a fixed deposit).

**Returns:**
- **Gross yield** = annual rent ÷ price.
- **Net yield (cap rate)** = NOI ÷ price (RE-M07-L02).
- **Cash-on-cash return** = annual cash flow after EMI ÷ own cash invested.
- **IRR (internal rate of return):** the yearly return that accounts for all cash in and out over time, including the final sale. In Sheets: `=IRR(range)`.

**Honest truth about small investors.** Returns often disappoint because of: high buying costs (10%+), low rental yields, vacancies, repairs, illiquidity (land can take months or years to sell), legal disputes, and buying at peaks. Many people count only the price rise and ignore costs, interest and time. Always compare with a simple alternative such as a fixed deposit or an index fund ([Personal Finance: gold, REITs and real estate](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m09-l06) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course)).

The full Cost and ROI calculators with working formulas are in the templates below and in your toolkit.

## Local example

**A rented house near Kuttiady, bought with a loan** (illustrative):
- Price ₹40 lakh; buying costs about ₹4.1 lakh; total ₹44.1 lakh.
- Rent ₹12,000 a month. Gross yield: 1,44,000 ÷ 40,00,000 = **3.6%**.
- NOI: rent for 11 months (1 vacant) ₹1,32,000, minus taxes ₹6,000, maintenance ₹20,000, insurance ₹3,000 = **₹1,03,000**. Net yield: **2.6%**.
- Loan ₹25 lakh at 8.5% for 20 years: EMI ≈ ₹21,700 (₹2.6 lakh a year).
- Own cash: 44.1 − 25 = ₹19.1 lakh. Cash flow: 1,03,000 − 2,60,400 ≈ **−₹1.57 lakh a year**. Cash-on-cash: **−8.2%**.
The owner pays ₹13,000 a month from salary and hopes prices rise. That is a bet on price growth, not an income investment.

**Land held for 5 years, no loan:** buy ₹20 lakh + ₹2.2 lakh costs = ₹22.2 lakh. Sell for ₹27 lakh after 5 years, minus 2% brokerage = ₹26.46 lakh. IRR ≈ **3.6% a year before capital gains tax**: likely less than a fixed deposit, and with much more risk.

## Worked calculation

**IRR in Sheets** for the land example: A1 `-2220000`, A2 to A5 `0` (or minus yearly land tax), A6 `2646000`. Then `=IRR(A1:A6)` ≈ 3.6%.
**Check by hand:** (26.46 ÷ 22.2) ^ (1/5) − 1 = 1.192 ^ 0.2 − 1 ≈ 0.036.
**Break-even rise needed** just to cover buying and selling costs: (22.2 ÷ 0.98) ÷ 20 − 1 ≈ **13.3%**.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Principles of Finance (OpenStax) on LibreTexts: chapter list including time value of money (chapters 7-9)](https://biz.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Finance/Principles_of_Finance_%28OpenStax%29) | Read the chapter on net present value and IRR in Principles of Finance | 30 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare 11.431J Real Estate Finance and Investment (Geltner and McGrath, CC BY-NC-SA)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/11-431j-real-estate-finance-and-investment-fall-2006) | Optional: lecture notes on investment returns | 20 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Square Yards (updated July 2026): stamp duty and registration charges in Kerala](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala) | Check current stamp duty for the cost tab | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Build the Cost and ROI tabs in your workbook from the templates.
2. Calculate the full cost of one purchase using current official stamp duty and fee rates (date-stamped) and real quotes for the writer's fee.
3. Choose 5 real properties (houses or shops for sale where you can estimate rent from local rental listings) and calculate gross yield, net yield, cash-on-cash (with and without a loan) and a 5-year IRR for each.
4. Write a half-page conclusion: which property type has the best yield locally, and how each compares with a fixed deposit rate you looked up.

**Proof to record:** The Cost tab for one purchase and the ROI tab for 5 properties with sources and dates, plus your conclusion.

**Full-time track:** Do 10 properties and add a sensitivity table (rent ±10%, price growth 0%, 3%, 6%).

## Template: Full cost of a purchase

```
FULL COST OF A PURCHASE (tab "Cost") - rates as of November 2026; check current rules
B1  Agreed price (Rs)                       [type]
B2  Fair value of the land/building (Rs)    [type, from the IGR fair value search]
B3  Value for duty = higher of the two      =MAX(B1,B2)
B4  Stamp duty rate                         0.08   (sale deed; check current rules)
B5  Registration fee rate                   0.02   (check current rules)
B6  Stamp duty (Rs)                         =B3*B4
B7  Registration fee (Rs)                   =B3*B5
B8  Document writer / advocate fee (Rs)     [type quote]
B9  EC, certified copies, sketches (Rs)     [type]
B10 Brokerage rate                          [type, e.g. 0.01 or 0.02]
B11 Brokerage (Rs)                          =B1*B10
B12 GST on brokerage (if charged)           =B11*0.18
B13 Loan processing fee and legal/valuation charges (Rs)  [type]
B14 Mutation, misc. travel (Rs)             [type]
B15 TOTAL extra costs                       =SUM(B6:B9,B11:B14)
B16 TOTAL cost of purchase                  =B1+B15
B17 Extra costs as % of price               =B15/B1
B18 TDS to deduct (if B1 or B2 is Rs 50 lakh or more) =IF(MAX(B1,B2)>=5000000, MAX(B1,B2)*0.01, 0)
(TDS is not an extra cost: it is part of the price paid to the government for the seller.)
```

## Template: Rental yield and return calculator

```
RENTAL YIELD AND RETURN CALCULATOR (tab "ROI")
B1  Purchase price (Rs)                 [type]
B2  Purchase costs (Rs)                 [from Cost tab B15]
B3  Total investment (Rs)               =B1+B2
B4  Monthly rent (Rs)                   [type]
B5  Gross annual rent                   =B4*12
B6  Gross rental yield                  =B5/B1
B7  Vacancy allowance (months a year)   [type, e.g. 1]
B8  Building tax + land tax per year    [type]
B9  Maintenance and repairs per year    [type, e.g. 1% of building value]
B10 Insurance and management fees       [type]
B11 Net operating income (NOI)          =B4*(12-B7)-B8-B9-B10
B12 Net yield / cap rate                =B11/B1
B13 Loan amount (Rs)                    [type, 0 if none]
B14 Annual interest rate                [type, e.g. 0.085]
B15 Loan term (years)                   [type]
B16 Monthly EMI                         =IF(B13>0, -PMT(B14/12, B15*12, B13), 0)
B17 Annual loan payments                =B16*12
B18 Cash invested (own money)           =B3-B13
B19 Annual cash flow after EMI          =B11-B17
B20 Cash-on-cash return                 =IF(B18>0, B19/B18, "")
IRR (tab "IRR"): list year 0 cash flow as minus own cash invested, then each
year's cash flow, and in the final year add the expected sale price minus
selling costs and loan balance. =IRR(B2:B12)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Counting only the price rise.** Include buying, owning and selling costs, interest and time.
- **Using asking rent.** Use actual rents from local listings and brokers.
- **Ignoring vacancy.** Allow at least one vacant month a year.

## Local fraud warning

**"Guaranteed return" schemes.** Some projects and agents promise guaranteed rent or returns ("12% assured"). Real property returns are not guaranteed; such promises are often unsustainable or fraudulent. Check who guarantees it, in writing, and with what assets.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. About how much do buying costs often add to a Kerala property's price?
    - A) 10% to 12%
    - B) 50%
    - C) 1%
    - D) Nothing
2. Rent ₹10,000 a month on a ₹30 lakh house. Gross yield?
    - A) 0.4%
    - B) 10%
    - C) 40%
    - D) 4%
3. What is cash-on-cash return?
    - A) Annual cash flow after EMI ÷ own cash invested
    - B) Price ÷ rent
    - C) Rent ÷ price
    - D) EMI ÷ rent
4. Why do many small investors earn less than expected?
    - A) There are no costs
    - B) High costs, low yields, vacancies, illiquidity and disputes
    - C) Property always doubles
    - D) Banks pay them
5. Which Sheets function gives IRR?
    - A) =MEDIAN()
    - B) =PMT()
    - C) =IRR(range)
    - D) =SUM()

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and both worked examples
- **Action:** calculate the full cost of one purchase and yield and returns for 5 real properties. It is done when your proof is saved: the Cost tab for one purchase and the ROI tab for 5 properties with sources and dates, plus your conclusion.
- **Quiz:** at least 4 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** 8% + 2% plus fees and brokerage.
2. **D.** 1,20,000 ÷ 30,00,000.
3. **A.** It shows the return on your own money.
4. **B.** Count everything.
5. **C.** List yearly cash flows first.

sections.title: Module 9: Property taxes
sections.summary: Property taxes: TDS on purchase, capital gains and exemptions, tax on rental income, tax on brokerage income, and GST on under-construction property and on brokerage services.
sections.content:
*Part B: Knowledge base.*

## Overview

The Income-tax Act, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026 and renumbered most sections, so this module describes rules by what they do. You will learn enough to warn clients and plan your own taxes, and always send real cases to a CA. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Explain TDS on property purchases.
- Work through a basic capital gains example and name the exemptions.
- Explain tax on rent and on your own service income.
- Explain when GST applies to property and brokerage.

## Time

About 3 hours in total: 2 hours 15 minutes of lessons and 45 minutes for the module project. Part-time: weeks 7–8, with the module project due in week 8.

## Lessons

1. RE-M09-L01: Taxes when buying and selling: TDS, capital gains and exemptions (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M09-L02: Tax on rent and brokerage, and GST (about 1 hour)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- TDS and LTCG formulas (RE-M09-L01).
- Tax questions for buyers and sellers (RE-M09-L01).
- Income and tax tracker (RE-M09-L02).

## Module project: a tax cheat sheet for clients and a tax plan for your business

1. Combine the TDS, capital gains, rental and GST rules into a one-page cheat sheet, each with its source and date.
2. Add your "tax questions to ask your CA" list.
3. Set up the Income tab and estimate your first-year tax position.
4. Have a CA check the cheat sheet for errors, if they agree.

**Proof to record:** The cheat sheet with sources and dates, and the Income tab.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Tax cheat sheet with sources and dates.
- Income tab for your business.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TDS | Unknown | Knows the 1% rule | Explains threshold, who deducts and the NRI exception |
| Capital gains | Unknown | Knows the rate | Works an example and names exemptions with limits |
| Rent and brokerage | Unknown | Knows they are taxed | Calculates house property income and own income |
| GST | Confused | Knows the 18% rate | Explains when GST applies and the registration threshold |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Learn the TDS and LTCG rules.
- Learn when GST applies.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| TDS on purchase | 1% if ₹50 lakh or more; buyer deducts. |
| TDS form under the 2025 Act | Form 141 (was 26QB); section 393 (reported). |
| LTCG on property | 12.5% without indexation. |
| Long-term holding | More than 24 months. |
| House reinvestment exemption cap | ₹10 crore. |
| House property deduction | 30% after municipal taxes. |
| GST on resale homes | None. |
| GST on brokerage | 18%; register above ₹20 lakh. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Using old section numbers without checking.** The 2025 Act renumbered them.
- **Advising on tax.** Send clients to a CA.
- **Ignoring your own taxes.** Track income and expenses from day 1.

sections.title: RE-M09-L01: Taxes when buying and selling: TDS, capital gains and exemptions
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can explain TDS on property purchases, how capital gains on property are taxed, and the main exemptions, and work through a simple example. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (25 minutes reading, 30 minutes on the worked example and action task).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Not tax advice.** The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 and renumbered most sections. This lesson describes rules by what they do, giving old and new section numbers only where a source was checked. A **chartered accountant (CA)** must advise on any real case. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

**TDS on buying property.** When the value of immovable property (other than agricultural land) is **₹50 lakh or more**, the **buyer** must deduct **1%** of the higher of the price or the stamp duty value as TDS, pay it to the government and give the seller a certificate. No TAN is needed; the buyer pays online with the seller's PAN ([Income Tax Department](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/w/tds-from-sum-paid-to-buy-an-immovable-property)). Under the 2025 Act this is reported as section 393 and the form as Form 141 (earlier Form 26QB) ([TaxGuru](https://taxguru.in/income-tax/tds-immovable-property-purchases-compliance-income-tax-act-2025.html)). If the seller is an **NRI**, much higher TDS rules apply and the buyer needs a TAN: always involve a CA.

TDS is **part of the price**, not an extra cost: on a ₹60 lakh house, the buyer pays ₹59.4 lakh to the seller and ₹60,000 to the government.

**Reporting.** Registration offices report property purchases above a threshold to the tax department (reported as ₹45 lakh from FY 2026-27, [Taxscan](https://www.taxscan.in/top-stories/property-transactions-and-income-tax-rules-in-india-compliance-essentials-for-fy-2026-27-1446927)). Undervalued deeds and cash deals are easily caught.

**Capital gains on selling property:**
| Rule | What it means | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Holding period for land and buildings | More than 24 months = long-term; otherwise short-term | Patron Accounting |
| Long-term capital gains (LTCG) rate | 12.5% without indexation (from 23 July 2024) | Housing.com |
| Choice for older property | Resident individuals and HUFs who bought before 23 July 2024 can choose 20% with indexation instead | Housing.com |
| Short-term gains | Added to income and taxed at slab rates | General rule; check with a CA |
| Reinvest in a house (old s.54, s.54F; s.54F is s.86 in the 2025 Act) | Buy a house 1 year before or 2 years after, or build within 3 years; exemption capped at ₹10 crore | Patron Accounting; Taxscan |
| Specified bonds (old s.54EC) | Invest gains from land or building within 6 months; up to ₹50 lakh a year; 5-year lock-in | Patron Accounting |

**How the gain is worked out (basic):** sale price (or stamp duty value, if higher) − selling costs (brokerage, legal) − cost of purchase (price plus stamp duty and registration paid) − cost of improvements = **capital gain**. With indexation (where chosen), the cost is raised using the government's cost inflation index.

**Inherited property:** the cost and holding period of the previous owner are generally used. Ask a CA.

**Agricultural land** in rural areas (outside specified distances from municipalities) is not a capital asset for tax; whether a Kerala village qualifies depends on population and distance rules; check current rules with a CA.

The [Personal Finance lesson on capital gains, TDS and advance tax](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m10-l03) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course) covers the general rules.

## Local example

**Selling a plot bought in 2018** (illustrative; ask a CA in a real case):
- Bought for ₹10 lakh in 2018; paid stamp duty and fee ₹1 lakh. Cost = ₹11 lakh.
- Sold in 2026 for ₹18 lakh; brokerage 2% = ₹36,000.
- Gain without indexation: 18,00,000 − 36,000 − 11,00,000 = **₹6,64,000**.
- Tax at 12.5% (plus cess): about **₹83,000** before cess.
- The seller, a resident individual who bought before 23 July 2024, can compare this with the 20%-with-indexation option and choose the lower tax.
- If the seller buys a house within the time limits, an exemption may apply (old section 54F for non-house assets, now section 86, if conditions are met).

Value was below ₹50 lakh, so the buyer did not deduct TDS.

## Worked calculation

**TDS in Sheets:** `=IF(MAX(B1,B2)>=5000000, MAX(B1,B2)*0.01, 0)` (B1 price, B2 stamp duty value).
**Simple LTCG (no indexation):** `=(sale - selling_costs - purchase_cost - improvements)*0.125`.
Add cess and compare the indexed option with a CA.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TDS on purchase | 1% if ₹50 lakh or more; buyer deducts; no TAN for resident sellers | Income Tax Department |
| TDS under the 2025 Act | Reported as section 393, Form 141 (was Form 26QB) | TaxGuru |
| LTCG | 12.5% without indexation; 20% with indexation option for property bought before 23 July 2024 | Housing.com |
| House reinvestment exemption | Capped at ₹10 crore; time limits apply | Patron Accounting, April 2026 |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Chartered accountant:** every capital gains calculation, exemptions, NRI sellers, inherited property and agricultural land status.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Income Tax Department: TDS on the sum paid to buy an immovable property](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/w/tds-from-sum-paid-to-buy-an-immovable-property) | Read the official TDS on property page | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [TaxGuru: TDS on immovable property purchases under the Income-tax Act, 2025](https://taxguru.in/income-tax/tds-immovable-property-purchases-compliance-income-tax-act-2025.html) | Read how TDS works under the 2025 Act | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Housing.com: LTCG on property, 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation](https://housing.com/news/fm-gives-choice-to-property-owners-20-ltcg-with-indexation-or-12-5-without-indexation) | Read the LTCG options | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Patron Accounting (updated 6 April 2026): capital gains exemptions, old sections 54, 54F and 54EC](https://www.patronaccounting.com/blog/capital-gains-exemption-section-54-54ec-54f) | Read the exemption conditions | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Add TDS and simple LTCG formulas to your Cost tab.
2. Work through the example above with a property price from your Comps sheet.
3. Ask one CA (or a tax practitioner) the three questions sellers most often get wrong about capital gains, and note their answers.
4. Write a "tax questions to ask your CA" sheet for clients.

**Proof to record:** The formulas, one worked example and notes from the CA conversation, plus your client sheet.

## Template: Tax questions for buyers and sellers

```
TAX QUESTIONS TO TAKE TO A CA (date ______; rules change)
BUYER
1 Is the value ₹50 lakh or more? -> TDS 1%; who files the form and when?
2 Is the seller an NRI? -> different TDS; TAN needed; CA must handle.
3 Any GST? (under-construction property from a builder)
SELLER
1 Bought when? held more than 24 months? cost including stamp duty?
2 LTCG at 12.5%, or 20% with indexation (bought before 23 July 2024)?
3 Planning to buy a house or bonds? time limits and caps?
4 Inherited? previous owner's cost and date?
5 Agricultural land: is it a capital asset in this village?
```

## Common mistakes

- **Treating TDS as an extra cost.** It is part of the price.
- **Forgetting stamp duty in the cost of purchase.** It is part of the cost.
- **Giving clients tax advice.** Explain the basics and send them to a CA.

## Local fraud warning

**"Show a lower price to save capital gains tax."** This is tax evasion. It also means the buyer's future cost is understated, so the buyer pays more tax later. Reporting systems catch many such deals.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Who deducts TDS on a property purchase of ₹50 lakh or more?
    - A) The broker
    - B) The seller
    - C) The buyer
    - D) The SRO
2. What is the LTCG rate on property without indexation?
    - A) 0%
    - B) 12.5%
    - C) 30%
    - D) 1%
3. How long must land be held for gains to be long-term?
    - A) 10 years
    - B) More than 24 months
    - C) 1 day
    - D) 6 months
4. Is TDS an extra cost to the buyer?
    - A) Only for flats
    - B) Yes
    - C) No, it is part of the price paid to the government for the seller
    - D) Only for NRIs

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the capital gains table
- **Action:** add TDS and LTCG formulas, work one example and talk to a CA. It is done when your proof is saved: the formulas, one worked example and notes from the CA conversation, plus your client sheet.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** 1% of the higher of price or stamp duty value.
2. **B.** From 23 July 2024.
3. **B.** For land and buildings.
4. **C.** The buyer pays less to the seller.

sections.title: RE-M09-L02: Tax on rent and brokerage, and GST
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can explain how rental income and brokerage income are taxed, when GST applies to property and to brokerage, and what records to keep. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 30 minutes on your own tax plan).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Not tax advice.** The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 and renumbered most sections. This lesson describes rules by what they do, giving old and new section numbers only where a source was checked. A **chartered accountant (CA)** must advise on any real case. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

**Tax on rental income (for your clients and your future self).**
- Rent from a house or shop is taxed as **income from house property**.
- From the annual rent, the owner deducts **municipal (building) taxes paid**, then a flat **30% standard deduction** for repairs; the new Act keeps this, applied after municipal taxes ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/tax/story/new-income-tax-bill-clarifies-key-deductions-on-house-property-income-489507-2025-08-14)). Interest on a loan for a let-out property can also be deducted (subject to limits and the regime chosen).
- Large rents paid by tenants may require the tenant to deduct TDS; ask a CA about current thresholds.

**Example:** annual rent ₹1,44,000; building tax ₹4,000; net annual value ₹1,40,000; 30% deduction ₹42,000; income from house property **₹98,000** (before loan interest), added to other income and taxed at slab rates.

**Tax on your brokerage or service income.**
- Commission from brokerage, property management or NRI property care is **business or professional income**, taxed at slab rates after allowable expenses (phone, travel, marketing). Keep receipts.
- Presumptive tax schemes may not apply to commission or brokerage income; ask a CA before using one (see the [Personal Finance lesson on freelancers and small businesses](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m10-l05) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course)).
- Builders or companies paying you commission may deduct TDS; it shows in your tax statement and you claim credit when filing.

**GST.**
- **Under-construction property** from a builder: GST **5%** on residential units (without input tax credit), **1%** on affordable housing (up to ₹45 lakh and up to 60 sq m carpet area in metros or 90 sq m elsewhere) ([Bajaj Finserv](https://www.bajajfinserv.in/reduction-in-gst-rate-on-housing); check current rules).
- **No GST** on completed property with an occupancy or completion certificate, or on resale between owners, or on land sales.
- **Brokerage and real estate services:** GST **18%**. GST registration is required once your turnover from services exceeds **₹20 lakh** a year (lower thresholds apply in some states; Kerala uses ₹20 lakh), or earlier if you choose to register ([Razorpay](https://razorpay.com/learn/gst-on-brokerage-and-commission/)). See also the [Entrepreneurship lesson on GST and income tax](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m08-l03) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course).

**Records to keep:** every invoice and receipt, bank statements, mandates and agreements, a simple income and expense sheet (RE-M20-L01).

## Local example

**Sachin's first year (illustrative):** commission from 6 rental deals (one month's rent each, average ₹9,000) = ₹54,000; 2 land sales at 2% of ₹15 lakh = ₹60,000; NRI property care for 3 owners at ₹1,500 a month = ₹54,000. Total ₹1,68,000.
- Expenses: phone and data ₹6,000, travel ₹18,000, printing and portal fees ₹4,000 = ₹28,000.
- Net professional income: **₹1,40,000**, added to any other income. With no other income, under the new regime this is likely below the taxable limit, but he still files a return to build a record (ask a CA).
- Turnover ₹1.68 lakh, far below ₹20 lakh, so GST registration is not required; he does not charge GST.

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| House property deduction | 30% standard deduction after municipal taxes, kept in the 2025 Act | Business Today |
| GST on under-construction homes | 5% (1% affordable); no GST on completed or resale property | Bajaj Finserv, July 2026 |
| GST on brokerage | 18%; registration above ₹20 lakh turnover | Razorpay |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Chartered accountant:** your own returns, whether to register for GST, TDS by tenants and any client's rental tax.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Business Today (14 August 2025): new Income-tax Bill keeps the 30% standard deduction on house property after municipal taxes](https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/tax/story/new-income-tax-bill-clarifies-key-deductions-on-house-property-income-489507-2025-08-14) | Read the house property rules | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Bajaj Finserv (July 2026): GST rates on housing](https://www.bajajfinserv.in/reduction-in-gst-rate-on-housing) | Read the GST rates on housing | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Razorpay: GST on brokerage and commission](https://razorpay.com/learn/gst-on-brokerage-and-commission/) | Read GST on brokerage and commission | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Work out the house property income for one rented property from your ROI tab.
2. Estimate your own first-year service income and expenses, as in the example, in an "Income" tab.
3. Check whether you would need GST registration.
4. Ask a CA (or tax practitioner) what records they want from a small broker each year, and note their answer.

**Proof to record:** The house property calculation, your income estimate and the CA's records list.

## Template: Income and tax tracker

```
INCOME AND TAX TRACKER (tab "Income")   Financial year ______
Date | Client | Deal | Invoice no. | Amount ₹ | Received by (UPI/bank) | TDS deducted? | Notes
EXPENSES: Date | Item | Amount | Receipt saved?
Totals: income =SUM(E:E)  expenses =SUM(...)  net =income-expenses
GST check: turnover this year =SUM(E:E); register if near ₹20 lakh (ask a CA)
Rental income (client or own): rent ______ - building tax ______ = NAV ______ ; 30% ______ ; taxable ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Charging GST without registration.** Only registered persons can collect GST.
- **Mixing personal and business money.** Use a separate account for business income.
- **Not keeping receipts.** Expenses without receipts are hard to claim.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake GST invoices.** Some people offer "GST bills" for a fee without real services. Using or issuing fake invoices is a serious offence. Issue invoices only for real services.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What deduction is allowed from rental income after municipal taxes?
    - A) A flat 30% standard deduction
    - B) 50%
    - C) Nothing
    - D) 100%
2. What GST applies to resale of a completed house between owners?
    - A) 12%
    - B) None
    - C) 5%
    - D) 18%
3. What GST rate applies to brokerage services?
    - A) 0%
    - B) 1%
    - C) 18%
    - D) 5%
4. When must a broker register for GST (services)?
    - A) Only for NRIs
    - B) When turnover exceeds ₹20 lakh a year (or voluntarily)
    - C) Never
    - D) From the first deal

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the GST rules
- **Action:** work out rental income tax for one property and your own first-year income and GST position. It is done when your proof is saved: the house property calculation, your income estimate and the CA's records list.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Kept in the 2025 Act.
2. **B.** GST applies to under-construction units from builders.
3. **C.** Once registered.
4. **B.** Check current thresholds.

sections.content:
*Part C: Run the business.*

## Overview

Part C is about running a legal real estate service business. It starts with doing things properly: registration when needed, written consent from owners and clear commission. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Explain when K-RERA registration is needed and how to apply.
- Follow the rules for registered agents.
- Use a written owner mandate with clear commission.
- Build a verified inventory.

## Time

About 3 hours 15 minutes in total: 2 hours 15 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: week 9, with the module project due in week 9.

## Lessons

1. RE-M10-L01: K-RERA agent registration and the rules agents must follow (about 1 hour)
2. RE-M10-L02: Owner mandates, commission and building an inventory (about 1 hour 15 minutes)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- K-RERA registration plan (RE-M10-L01).
- Owner mandate template (RE-M10-L02).
- Inventory tab (RE-M10-L02).

## Module project: your agent starter pack

1. Registration plan with current K-RERA process notes.
2. Advocate-reviewed (or ready to review) mandate template.
3. At least one signed mandate and the Inventory tab.
4. A one-paragraph "how I work" statement (consent, honesty, no cash, privacy) for owners and clients.

**Proof to record:** The four items (owner details private).

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Owner mandate template.
- Inventory tab with expiry alerts.
- Registration plan.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Registration | Not considered | Knows the rules | Dated plan with documents and timing |
| Mandates | Verbal only | Template ready | Signed mandate in use |
| Commission | Unclear | Range known | Written, disclosed and paid by bank transfer |
| Inventory | None | Unverified list | Verified, mandated properties with expiry alerts |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Read the K-RERA agent rules.
- Sign one mandate.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| K-RERA agent form | Form G. |
| Agent fee (individual) | ₹25,000 (reported). |
| Registration needed for | Sales in RERA-registered projects. |
| Mandate | Owner's written authorisation to market. |
| Who sets the final price? | The owner. |
| Sale commission (common) | 1% to 2%; agree in writing. |
| Rental commission (common) | About one month's rent. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Skipping paperwork to move fast.** Paperwork protects you.
- **Promising owners unrealistic prices to win mandates.** Use your comparables.
- **Ignoring mandate expiry.** Renew or close.

sections.title: RE-M10-L01: K-RERA agent registration and the rules agents must follow
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can explain when you need K-RERA agent registration, how to apply, what it costs and the rules a registered agent must follow. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 30 minutes on the K-RERA site and your registration plan).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Do you need to register?** Under the RERA Act, anyone who acts as an agent for the sale of plots, apartments or buildings in a **RERA-registered project** must register with the state authority before doing so (RE-M04-L02). Resale of individual properties between owners and rentals are generally outside RERA, but registering early:
- lets you work with builders and project sales;
- shows clients you are accountable;
- puts your registration number on your cards, listings and agreements.

**How to apply in Kerala** (from K-RERA and secondary guides; check current rules on the [K-RERA site](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) before applying):
- Application in **Form G** under the Kerala RERA rules ([TaxGuru](https://taxguru.in/corporate-law/kerala-rera-rules-registration.html)).
- Reported documents: PAN, address proof, two passport photos, business address proof, registration certificate (for a firm or company) and **income tax returns for the previous three years** ([Square Yards, November 2024](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/rera-kerala-rerat)). If you haven't filed returns, ask K-RERA what they accept and start filing now.
- Fee: **₹25,000** for an individual; ₹2 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh for others (sources differ) ([TaxGuru](https://taxguru.in/corporate-law/kerala-rera-rules-registration.html); [Onmanorama](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2020/01/01/rera-real-estate-regulatory-authority-norms.html)).
- The procedure was reported as offline (by post) in late 2024; check whether an online option exists now.
- Registration is valid for a fixed period and must be renewed (renewal Form J); check the current period and fee.

**Rules registered agents must follow** (RERA Act, as summarised by [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Estate_%28Regulation_and_Development%29_Act,_2016)):
- Don't facilitate sales in unregistered projects that must be registered.
- Quote your registration number in every advert and deal.
- Keep books of account, records and documents.
- Don't make false statements about a project or property, and don't use unfair trade practices.
- Help buyers get the information and documents they are entitled to.
- Penalties for agents who don't register: reported **₹10,000 a day** ([Onmanorama](https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2020/01/01/rera-real-estate-regulatory-authority-norms.html)).

**When to register:** the ₹25,000 fee is significant on a small budget. A sensible path: start with rentals, resale and NRI property care (no RERA registration needed), file your tax returns, then register before you handle any project sales.

## Local example

Sachin's plan:
- Months 1 to 6: rentals and resale only; no project sales. File his income tax return for the year, even if income is low.
- Month 6: a builder in Kuttiady offers him 1.5% commission to sell flats in a 24-flat registered project. He tells the builder he will apply for K-RERA registration first and will not advertise the project until he has his number.
- He prepares Form G, documents and the ₹25,000 fee (from his first commissions), and adds a line to his cards: "K-RERA agent registration no. ______".

## Key rules (as of November 2026)

Laws, rates and portals change. Each rule below was checked against the source shown on 2026-11-04; **check current rules** before you rely on it.

| Rule | What it means in practice | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent registration form | Form G under the Kerala RERA rules | TaxGuru; Square Yards |
| Agent fee | Individual ₹25,000; others ₹2 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh (sources differ) | TaxGuru; Onmanorama |
| Documents (reported) | PAN, address proof, photos, business address, ITRs for 3 years | Square Yards, November 2024 |
| Penalty for not registering | Reported ₹10,000 per day | Onmanorama |

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate or CA:** if you form a firm or company for the agency, or need help with the application.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Find the agent registration page, forms and the list of registered agents | 20 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Square Yards (updated 22 November 2024): RERA Kerala agent registration, Form G and documents](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/rera-kerala-rerat) | Read the documents list and steps | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [TaxGuru: Kerala RERA Rules, registration fees](https://taxguru.in/corporate-law/kerala-rera-rules-registration.html) | Read the fee table | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. On the K-RERA site, find the current agent registration process and forms, and note the date you checked.
2. List the documents you have and those you still need (ITRs, address proof).
3. Count the registered agents in Kozhikode district and look at two of their public profiles.
4. Write your registration plan: when you will register, how you will pay the fee and what you will do before then.

**Proof to record:** Notes on the current process with the date, your documents list and your registration plan.

## Template: K-RERA agent registration plan

```
K-RERA AGENT REGISTRATION PLAN      checked on ______ at rera.kerala.gov.in
Process: offline / online ______   Form: G   Renewal form: J
Fee (individual): ₹ ______ (reported ₹25,000)   Validity: ______ years
Documents:  PAN [ ]  address proof [ ]  2 photos [ ]  business address proof [ ]
            ITR year 1 [ ] year 2 [ ] year 3 [ ]  (firm: registration certificate [ ])
Before registering I will only do: rentals / resale / NRI care / marketing services
I will register by: ______ (before any project sale)
After registering: number on cards, listings, mandates, website [ ]
```

## Common mistakes

- **Selling project units before registering.** Register first; penalties are heavy.
- **Not filing income tax returns.** Returns are needed for registration and loans.
- **Assuming registration means you can draft documents.** It doesn't; drafting is for document writers and advocates.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake RERA agents.** Some people print made-up K-RERA numbers on cards. Clients can search the agent list; make sure your own number is real and visible, and check other agents' numbers before working with them.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. When must an agent register with K-RERA?
    - A) Never
    - B) Only after 10 deals
    - C) Before facilitating sales in RERA-registered projects
    - D) Only for rentals
2. What is the reported K-RERA fee for an individual agent?
    - A) ₹25,000
    - B) ₹2,50,000
    - C) Free
    - D) ₹500
3. Which document is reported as required that many beginners lack?
    - A) A car licence
    - B) A degree certificate
    - C) A passport
    - D) Income tax returns for the previous three years
4. What must a registered agent show in adverts?
    - A) Nothing
    - B) Their home address
    - C) Their bank balance
    - D) Their K-RERA registration number

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the K-RERA agent pages
- **Action:** check the current K-RERA process and write your registration plan. It is done when your proof is saved: notes on the current process with the date, your documents list and your registration plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Resale and rentals are generally outside RERA.
2. **A.** Firms pay more.
3. **D.** Start filing returns now.
4. **D.** It's required.

sections.title: RE-M10-L02: Owner mandates, commission and building an inventory
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can get a written owner mandate, agree commission clearly and build an inventory of properties with complete, verified information. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (20 minutes reading, 55 minutes on mandates and inventory).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Why a written mandate.** A mandate (authorisation) from the owner proves you have permission to market the property, sets the commission and avoids disputes ("I never asked you to sell"). Without one, you risk misrepresenting a property you don't control, working for nothing or falling out with the owner. The rule is simple: **act only with the owner's consent, in writing.**

**What a mandate covers** (toolkit template below; have an advocate review your version):
- Property details as in the deed.
- Sale or rent; exclusive or not; period (for example 90 days).
- Asking price and who decides the final price (the owner).
- Commission: amount, when it is due (on registration or on signing the rental agreement) and payment by bank transfer.
- Owner's confirmation that they have the right to sell and that the information is true.
- Your duties: honest marketing, sharing all offers in writing, privacy, no money collected without written approval.
- Where photos and videos may be published.

**Commission norms in Kerala** (practice varies; confirm in your broker interviews):
| Deal | Common practice | How to handle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Land or house sale | Commonly 1% to 2% of the price from the seller, sometimes also from the buyer | Must be agreed in writing; disclose if you take from both |
| House or shop rental | Commonly one month's rent (or half from each side) | Agree who pays before showing |
| Project flats (builder) | Percentage paid by the builder (needs K-RERA registration) | Builder agreement; TDS may be deducted |
| NRI property care | Monthly fee per property | Written service agreement (RE-M15-L02) |
Write the commission in the mandate and in a short note to the buyer or tenant if they also pay. Never hide commission from either side.

**Building an inventory.** Your inventory is your stock of properties you are allowed to market. For each property: owner's mandate, verified documents summary, photos, price, key facts and status. Keep it in an "Inventory" tab (columns similar to the Comps sheet, plus mandate date, expiry and status). Quality beats quantity: 10 properties with verified papers and mandates are worth more than 50 rumours.

## Local example

An owner in Thottilpalam wants to sell 15 cents with a house. Sachin meets him, reads the deed and tax receipt, and explains his service. They agree:
- Non-exclusive mandate for 90 days; asking ₹38 lakh; the owner decides the final price.
- Commission 2% of the final price on registration, by bank transfer.
- Photos and video can go on NoBroker, Facebook and Sachin's WhatsApp channel; no house number or owner's phone number in public.
- The owner signs; Sachin keeps a copy and adds the property to his Inventory tab with the mandate expiry date.
If a buyer is found at ₹36 lakh, commission is 36,00,000 × 0.02 = **₹72,000**, invoiced after registration.

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** reviews your standard mandate template once, and any unusual terms.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Check whether K-RERA publishes any agent code of conduct or forms you should follow | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [NoBroker: list your property for rent or sale (free for owners)](https://www.nobroker.in/list-your-property-for-rent-sale) | See how owner listings describe properties (for inventory fields) | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Adapt the mandate template with your details and have it reviewed by an advocate (or note that you will before first use).
2. Ask your interviewed brokers what commission they charge for sales and rentals, and note the range.
3. Approach 2 to 3 owners you know (family, neighbours) who want to sell or let; with consent, sign a mandate with at least one.
4. Set up the Inventory tab and add each mandated property with full details.

**Proof to record:** Your mandate template, commission notes from brokers, at least one signed mandate (private) and the Inventory tab.

## Template: Owner mandate template

```
OWNER MANDATE (agreement to market a property) - review with an advocate before use
This agreement is made on ______ at ______ between:
OWNER: ______ (address ______, phone ______) and
AGENT: ______ (K-RERA agent registration no. ______, if registered; address ______)
1. Property: survey no. ______, ______ village, ______ taluk, area ______ cents,
   building ______ sq ft, as per title deed no. ______ of ______ SRO.
2. Purpose: the owner authorises the agent to market the property for SALE / RENT.
3. Type: exclusive / non-exclusive. Period: from ______ to ______ (e.g. 90 days).
4. Asking price / rent: Rs ______. Minimum acceptable: to be decided by the owner only.
5. Commission: ______% of the final sale price (or ___ month's rent), payable by the
   owner only on registration of the sale deed / signing of the rental agreement,
   by bank transfer, with a GST invoice if the agent is GST-registered.
6. The owner confirms that the information given is true and that they have the
   right to sell / let. The agent will not publish anything the owner has not approved.
7. The agent will: market honestly, share all offers in writing, not take money from
   buyers on the owner's behalf without written approval, and keep documents private.
8. Photos and videos may be published on: ______ (portals / social media).
9. Either party may end this agreement with ___ days' written notice.
Owner signature ______  Agent signature ______  Witnesses 1 ______ 2 ______
```

## Template: Inventory tab

```
INVENTORY (tab "Inventory")
ID | Owner (private) | Mandate date | Mandate expiry | Exclusive? | Type | Locality | Cents | Sq ft | Asking ₹ | Docs checked (Y/partial/N) | Photos (Y/N) | Listed where | Status (active/under offer/sold/let/withdrawn) | Notes
Expiry alert: =IF(D2-TODAY()<=14,"RENEW OR CLOSE","")
Rule: no listing goes public without a signed mandate and owner-approved text and photos.
```

## Common mistakes

- **Marketing on a verbal "OK".** Get it in writing, even a signed short mandate.
- **Unclear commission.** Write the amount, timing and payment mode.
- **Collecting big inventories of unverified properties.** Fewer, verified, mandated properties.

## Local fraud warning

**Listing without consent.** Some brokers copy listings from portals or WhatsApp groups and advertise them as their own. It misleads buyers, angers owners and breaks trust. Only market properties you hold a mandate for, or co-broke openly with the broker who does.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Why get a written owner mandate?
    - A) It replaces the sale deed
    - B) It transfers ownership
    - C) It proves consent, sets commission and prevents disputes
    - D) It is only for NRIs
2. Who decides the final sale price?
    - A) The neighbour
    - B) The broker
    - C) The buyer alone
    - D) The owner
3. What is commonly charged for a house rental in Kerala?
    - A) Nothing
    - B) 10% of property value
    - C) About one month's rent
    - D) One year's rent
4. If you take commission from both buyer and seller, what must you do?
    - A) Nothing
    - B) Hide it
    - C) Disclose it to both in writing
    - D) Charge double secretly

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the mandate template
- **Action:** adapt the mandate, sign at least one with an owner and set up your inventory. It is done when your proof is saved: your mandate template, commission notes from brokers, at least one signed mandate (private) and the Inventory tab.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Act only with written consent.
2. **D.** The broker advises; the owner decides.
3. **C.** Practice varies; confirm locally.
4. **C.** Transparency avoids conflicts.

*Part C: Run the business.*

## Overview

The practical heart of this module is the interviews: 3 local brokers and 1 document writer or advocate. They will teach you more about the Kuttiady and Kozhikode market than any website. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Build a local and NRI network with consent.
- Interview brokers and professionals and learn the local market.
- Source from builders and online channels.
- Grade and track leads by source.

## Time

About 3 hours 15 minutes in total: 2 hours 15 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 9–10, with the module project due in week 10.

## Lessons

1. RE-M11-L01: Local and NRI networks, and learning from local brokers (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M11-L02: Builders, online sources and lead quality (about 1 hour)
