sections.title: Module 19: Tech and AI in real estate
sections.summary: Tech and AI in real estate: a free CRM in Google Sheets or LibreOffice, maps with Google Earth and QGIS, and AI tools for listings, analysis and communication, used safely and honestly.
sections.content:
*Part C: Run the business.*

## Overview

Everything here works on an Android phone and an old laptop with free tools. The practical milestone is a CRM in daily use with every lead tracked. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Build and use a CRM with formulas and a dashboard.
- Map listings with Google Earth or QGIS.
- Use AI tools for drafts and analysis with clear rules.
- Protect client data.

## Time

About 2 hours 45 minutes in total: 2 hours of lessons and 45 minutes for the module project. Part-time: week 14, with the module project due in week 14.

## Lessons

1. RE-M19-L01: A CRM in Google Sheets (about 1 hour)
2. RE-M19-L02: Maps, GIS and AI tools (about 1 hour)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- CRM sheet and dashboard formulas (RE-M19-L01).
- AI prompt starters and rules (RE-M19-L02).

## Module project: your digital toolkit in use

1. CRM with all leads and next actions, used daily for two weeks.
2. Dashboard with conversion by source.
3. Price map of 20+ listings.
4. Your AI rules and two edited AI drafts.

**Proof to record:** Screenshots (personal details blurred), the map and your AI rules.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- CRM (Leads tab) and Dashboard.
- Price map.
- AI prompt starters and rules.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CRM | Not used | Set up | Used daily with next actions and dashboard |
| Maps | None | Google Earth views | Price map of 20+ listings |
| AI | Unchecked drafts | Edited drafts | Edited, fact-checked drafts and written rules |
| Privacy | Public sheet or shared data | Private sheet | Private, 2-step verified, consent recorded |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Build the Leads tab with the overdue formula.
- Write your AI rules.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| CRM | Track every lead, stage and next action. |
| Overdue flag | Next action date before today and not closed or lost. |
| Conversion rate | Closed ÷ total leads. |
| QGIS | Free, open-source GIS. |
| Google Earth Pro desktop download | Ending 25 June 2027 (announced). |
| AI rule 1 | Verify every law, rate and number. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Buying software too early.** Free sheets are enough to start.
- **Not updating the CRM.** Daily 10-minute habit.
- **Letting AI write unchecked content.** You are responsible for every word.

sections.title: RE-M19-L01: A CRM in Google Sheets
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can build and use a free CRM in Google Sheets (or LibreOffice) that tracks every lead, property and follow-up, with formulas for overdue actions and conversion. **Time:** about 1 hour (15 minutes reading, 45 minutes building and using the CRM).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Why a CRM.** Deals in real estate take weeks or months, and leads go cold if you forget them. A simple **CRM (customer relationship management) sheet** is enough for a beginner and works on your phone ([Google Sheets](https://workspace.google.com/products/sheets/)) and old laptop ([LibreOffice Calc](https://www.libreoffice.org/)).

**Your workbook tabs (built through the course):** Comps, Cost, ROI, Loan, Inventory, **Leads**, Network, Income, Log. The Leads tab is your CRM; its header row and formulas are in the templates below.

**Making it work:**
- **Data validation** (drop-down lists) for Stage, Source and Type so the counts work.
- **Conditional formatting:** colour overdue follow-ups red, hot leads green.
- **Filter views:** "today's follow-ups", "hot leads", "properties under offer".
- **Link leads to properties:** use your Inventory IDs in "Properties shown".
- **Daily habit (10 minutes):** check overdue actions, update stages after every call or visit, set a next action date for every open lead.
- **Weekly (in your log):** count leads, visits and deals by source (RE-M11-L02).

**A weekly pipeline review (15 minutes, Sunday with your log):**
1. Sort by Stage. For each lead at "visited" or "offer", ask: what is the one next step, and who owns it?
2. Move leads with no response after three polite follow-ups to "lost", with a reason (price, location, bought elsewhere, not serious). The reasons teach you what the market wants.
3. Check the Inventory tab: mandates expiring in the next two weeks, listings to refresh, properties with no enquiries for a month (talk to the owner about price, using your comparables).
4. Write the week's three actions in your log.

**When to move beyond a sheet.** A sheet works well up to a few hundred leads. If you later hire people or handle many projects, a dedicated CRM may help, but only after your process works on the sheet. Choose one that lets you export your data and that keeps client data secure.

**Privacy and security:** keep the sheet private (not "anyone with the link"); use a strong password and two-step verification on your Google account; record consent; delete details of people who ask, and of leads that are closed or lost after a reasonable time; never share client data with others without consent.

## Local example

After two months Sachin's Leads tab has 48 rows. His Dashboard tab shows: new 9, contacted 14, visit booked 4, visited 11, offer 2, agreement 1, closed 4, lost 3. Overdue follow-ups: 6 (red). Conversion: 4 ÷ 48 ≈ **8%**. By source: referrals 15 leads → 3 closed; NoBroker 12 → 1 closed; Facebook 11 → 0 closed.
He changes his week: more time with referral partners, fewer Facebook posts, and a rule that every visited lead gets a follow-up within 48 hours.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Sheets (free with a Google account; works on phones and offline)](https://workspace.google.com/products/sheets/) | Set up the workbook and install the phone app | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [LibreOffice (free and open source; Calc spreadsheet works on an old laptop)](https://www.libreoffice.org/) | Optional: install Calc on the laptop for offline work | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Create the Leads tab with the header row, drop-down lists for Stage, Source and Type, and the overdue formula.
2. Enter every current lead (with consent) and set a next action date for each open one.
3. Build a Dashboard tab with counts by stage and source, and the conversion rate.
4. Use the CRM daily for two weeks and note how many follow-ups you completed on time.

**Proof to record:** A CRM screenshot with personal details blurred, the dashboard and your two-week follow-up count.

## Template: CRM sheet

```
Lead ID,Date,Name,Phone,Source,Buy/Rent/Sell/Let,Type,Area wanted,Budget (Rs),Stage (new/contacted/visit booked/visited/offer/agreement/closed/lost),Next action,Next action date,Properties shown,Notes,Consent (Y/N)

CRM SHEET (tab "Leads"). Row 1 = headers above.
Overdue follow-ups: add column P "Overdue?" with =IF(AND(L2<>"", L2<TODAY(), J2<>"closed", J2<>"lost"),"OVERDUE","")
Pipeline count by stage (on a "Dashboard" tab): =COUNTIF(Leads!J:J,"visited")
Conversion rate: =COUNTIF(Leads!J:J,"closed")/COUNTA(Leads!A2:A)
Use Data > Data validation on column J so stages are always spelled the same.
```

## Template: Dashboard formulas

```
DASHBOARD (tab "Dashboard")
Leads total:         =COUNTA(Leads!A2:A)
By stage (A2 list of stages, B2): =COUNTIF(Leads!J:J,A2)
By source (D2 list of sources, E2): =COUNTIF(Leads!E:E,D2)   closed: =COUNTIFS(Leads!E:E,D2,Leads!J:J,"closed")
Overdue follow-ups:  =COUNTIF(Leads!P:P,"OVERDUE")
Conversion:          =COUNTIF(Leads!J:J,"closed")/COUNTA(Leads!A2:A)
Commission this year: =SUM(Income!E:E)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Free-text stages.** Use drop-down lists so counts work.
- **Leads without next action dates.** Every open lead gets a date.
- **Sharing the sheet publicly.** Keep it private and secure.

## Local fraud warning

**Data theft.** Client lists are valuable to scammers. Don't share login details, don't install unknown "CRM" apps that ask for full access to your contacts, and turn on two-step verification.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Why use drop-down lists in the CRM?
    - A) To slow you down
    - B) For colour
    - C) So stages and sources are spelled the same and counts work
    - D) It is required by law
2. What must every open lead have?
    - A) A next action date
    - B) A token advance
    - C) A photo
    - D) Nothing
3. Which formula flags overdue follow-ups?
    - A) =MEDIAN(L2)
    - B) =SUM(L2)
    - C) =IF(AND(L2<>"", L2<TODAY(), J2<>"closed", J2<>"lost"),"OVERDUE","")
    - D) =PMT(L2)
4. How should the CRM sheet be shared?
    - A) Printed and left at the office
    - B) Privately, with two-step verification on the account
    - C) Anyone with the link
    - D) Posted in groups

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the CRM formulas
- **Action:** build the CRM and dashboard and use them daily for two weeks. It is done when your proof is saved: a CRM screenshot with personal details blurred, the dashboard and your two-week follow-up count.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Clean data.
2. **A.** Prevents forgotten leads.
3. **C.** Compares the date with today.
4. **B.** Protect client data.

sections.title: RE-M19-L02: Maps, GIS and AI tools
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can use Google Earth, QGIS and AI tools for property research, listings, analysis and communication, safely and honestly. **Time:** about 1 hour (15 minutes reading, 45 minutes of practice).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Google Earth** ([versions](https://www.google.com/earth/about/versions/)): web and mobile apps let you view plots, measure distances and areas roughly, see surroundings (rivers, slopes, quarries) and historical imagery (in Earth Pro). Google has said the Earth Pro desktop download will end on 25 June 2027; check what remains available (check current rules). Use it to: draw a plot boundary for a virtual tour, measure distance to the road and town, and check flood-prone low land near rivers.

**QGIS** ([QGIS](https://qgis.org/)): free, open-source GIS (GPL). It can run on an older laptop for small projects. Uses for you: overlay your listings (from the Comps sheet as a CSV with coordinates) on a map, add the KSDMA hazard map layers if available ([KSDMA](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/hazard-maps/)), and make a simple price map by locality. Start small: load a CSV of 20 listings with latitude and longitude and colour them by price per cent.

**AI tools** (free tiers of general assistants) can help with:
- **Listings:** turning your notes into clear English and Malayalam drafts (then you edit for accuracy).
- **Analysis:** explaining formulas, checking your spreadsheet logic, summarising your market notes.
- **Communication:** polite follow-up messages, explaining a process to an NRI client in simple words, translating.
- **Learning:** quizzing yourself on this course.

**Rules for AI use:**
| Area | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Facts | AI tools can invent laws, rates and section numbers. Check every legal or numeric claim against official sources |
| Privacy | Don't paste clients' names, phone numbers, ID numbers or documents into AI tools |
| Honesty | AI-written listings must still be true; edit out hype and anything you can't verify |
| Disclosure | Don't use AI to fake reviews, testimonials or photos (no AI-generated "photos" of a real property) |
| Advice | AI is not an advocate, surveyor, CA or valuer |

The [Entrepreneurship lesson on AI for research and marketing](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m11-l01) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course) and the [Social Media Marketing lesson on AI for content](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/social-media-marketing/smm-m13-l01) (in the Practical Social Media Marketing course) cover more uses.

## Local example

Sachin types his notes for a plot into an AI assistant (no names or numbers): "10 cents, 4 m panchayat road, 2 km Kuttiady, level, well, part slopes at back, price 2.2 lakh per cent". He asks for a 4-line English listing and a Malayalam version. The draft says "prime investment opportunity with excellent appreciation": he deletes it, because he can't promise that, and adds "back 2 cents slope". He then asks the AI to explain how to colour points by value in QGIS, and checks the steps against the QGIS documentation.

In QGIS he loads his 24 listings (CSV with coordinates from Google Maps pins) and colours them by price per cent: the map shows prices dropping sharply beyond 3 km from Kuttiady town, which matches what brokers told him.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [QGIS: free and open-source GIS (GPL)](https://qgis.org/) | Download QGIS (long-term release) and load a CSV of points | 30 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Google Earth versions (web, mobile, Pro desktop)](https://www.google.com/earth/about/versions/) | Measure a plot and draw its boundary | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Kerala State Disaster Management Authority: hazard maps (flood, landslide)](https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/hazard-maps/) | Hazard maps to compare with your listings | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Add latitude and longitude to 20 listings in your Comps sheet (from map pins you are allowed to use) and export them as CSV.
2. Load them in QGIS (or Google Earth/My Maps if your laptop can't run QGIS) and colour by price per cent.
3. Use an AI assistant to draft one listing and one client message from your notes (no personal data), then edit and fact-check.
4. Write your own AI use rules (5 lines) for your business.

**Proof to record:** The price map screenshot, the AI draft and your edited version side by side, and your AI rules.

## Template: AI prompt starters and rules

```
AI PROMPT STARTERS (never include names, phone numbers, ID or document numbers)
Listing: "Turn these facts into a 4-line honest listing in English and simple Malayalam. Do not add claims I didn't give. Facts: ..."
Message: "Write a polite WhatsApp follow-up to a buyer who visited a plot 3 days ago. Ask if they have questions. 3 lines."
Explain: "Explain to an NRI client in simple English what an encumbrance certificate shows and doesn't show."
Check: "Find errors in this formula: ..."
MY AI RULES
1 Check every law, rate and number against official sources.  2 No personal data in AI tools.
3 Edit out hype and unverifiable claims.  4 No fake photos, reviews or testimonials.
5 AI is not my advocate, surveyor, CA or valuer.
```

## Common mistakes

- **Trusting AI for legal facts.** Verify with official sources.
- **Pasting client documents into AI tools.** Never share personal data.
- **Using AI-generated images of properties.** Only real photos.

## Local fraud warning

**AI-faked documents and photos.** AI makes it easier to fake deeds, ECs, certificates and photos. Always get documents from official sources yourself, and visit properties in person.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What should you never paste into an AI tool?
    - A) Clients' names, phone numbers, IDs or documents
    - B) Road width
    - C) Plot size
    - D) A formula
2. An AI draft says "guaranteed appreciation". You:
    - A) Keep it
    - B) Add more hype
    - C) Delete it; you can't promise that
    - D) Make it bigger
3. What is QGIS?
    - A) Free, open-source GIS software
    - B) A property portal
    - C) A government office
    - D) A bank
4. Why check AI answers on laws and rates?
    - A) AI can invent laws, rates and section numbers
    - B) It is always right
    - C) Only for fun
    - D) It is not necessary

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the AI rules
- **Action:** make a price map of 20 listings and use AI safely for one listing and one message. It is done when your proof is saved: the price map screenshot, the AI draft and your edited version side by side, and your AI rules.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Privacy.
2. **C.** Honest listings.
3. **A.** GPL licensed.
4. **A.** Verify with official sources.

sections.summary: Setting up your business: structure, registrations, GST, bookkeeping, pricing, partnerships, co-broking and growing from a solo broker into a small agency.
sections.content:
*Part C: Run the business.*

## Overview

This module turns your skills into a legal, organised business. It builds on the Entrepreneurship course rather than repeating it. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Choose a structure and plan registrations.
- Keep simple, accurate books.
- Price services and set fair partnerships.
- Plan 12 months of growth.

## Time

About 3 hours in total: 2 hours of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 14–15, with the module project due in week 15.

## Lessons

1. RE-M20-L01: Structure, registration, GST and bookkeeping (about 1 hour)
2. RE-M20-L02: Pricing your services, partnerships and growing an agency (about 1 hour)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- Business set-up checklist (RE-M20-L01).
- Rate card and 12-month plan (RE-M20-L02).

## Module project: your business set-up and 12-month plan

1. Set-up checklist with dates.
2. Income and Expenses tabs in use.
3. Rate card, co-broking outline and referral policy.
4. 12-month plan with targets and growth steps.

**Proof to record:** The four items.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Business set-up checklist.
- Rate card.
- 12-month plan.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Set-up | Not started | Some items | Dated checklist with each item decided |
| Books | None | Partial | Income, expenses, invoices and monthly reconciliation |
| Pricing | Unclear | Rates known | Rate card based on local evidence |
| Growth | No plan | Targets only | Monthly targets, expenses, buffer and growth steps |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Choose a structure and open a separate account.
- Write your rate card.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Beginner structure | Sole proprietorship. |
| Separate account | Business money apart from personal and client money. |
| Invoice numbering | RE-2026-001, 002, ... |
| Co-broking | Written split, disclosed to clients. |
| Referral fees | Disclosed in writing; never affect advice. |
| Buffer | 3 to 6 months of expenses. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Ignoring the paperwork side of the business.** Set it up early.
- **Growth before quality.** Reputation first.
- **No review of targets.** Review monthly against the CRM.

sections.title: RE-M20-L01: Structure, registration, GST and bookkeeping
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can choose a business structure, list the registrations you need and when, and keep simple, accurate books for a real estate service business. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes on your set-up checklist and books).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Choosing a structure:**
| Structure | What it is | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sole proprietorship | You alone; simplest; no separate registration of the business itself | Unlimited personal liability; good to start |
| Partnership firm | Two or more partners with a written (preferably registered) partnership deed | Shared liability; disputes common without a clear deed |
| LLP | Limited liability partnership registered with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs | Limited liability; annual filings and costs |
| Private limited company | Separate company; directors and shareholders | Most compliance; for larger agencies or development |
For a beginner working alone, a **sole proprietorship** is usually enough. Move to a partnership or LLP when you work with partners, and only with an advocate-drafted agreement. The [Entrepreneurship lesson on business structures](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m09-l01) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course) goes into detail.

**Registrations and when you need them** (check current rules with your panchayat, a CA and the [Entrepreneurship lesson on registrations in Kerala](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m09-l02) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course)):
| Item | What it is | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PAN and bank account | A separate bank account (savings at first, current account later) for business income and expenses | From day 1 |
| Income tax returns | File every year, even with small income; needed for K-RERA registration and loans | From year 1 |
| K-RERA agent registration | Before handling sales in registered projects (RE-M10-L01) | When you start project sales |
| Udyam registration | Free online MSME registration; useful for some schemes and bank relationships | Optional, early |
| Local body trade licence / Shops and Establishments registration | If you open an office or shop; requirements vary | When you have premises; ask your panchayat |
| GST registration | Required above ₹20 lakh service turnover, or voluntarily (RE-M09-L02) | When turnover approaches the limit |

**Bookkeeping (simple and accurate):**
- One **Income** tab (RE-M09-L02) and one **Expenses** tab; every entry with date, client or vendor, amount, mode and receipt or invoice number.
- Number your invoices (RE-2026-001, RE-2026-002…).
- Keep receipts as photos in a folder by month.
- Reconcile with the bank statement monthly.
- Never mix owners' or clients' money with yours; if you hold any client money, use a separate account and record it separately.
- Monthly profit: income − expenses. Set aside money for tax.
See the [Entrepreneurship lesson on bookkeeping and cash flow](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m08-l01) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course).

**Insurance and safety:** consider personal accident cover and phone and data backups. Keep copies of every mandate and agreement.

**Your business name and identity:** a clear name, a professional email (free), a WhatsApp Business profile, a Google Business Profile and simple visiting cards that show your K-RERA number once registered, and your money rules (RE-M04-L05).

## Local example

Sachin's set-up (month 1):
- Sole proprietor; trade name "Sachin Property Services, Kuttiady".
- PAN (has one); a separate savings account for business; files his income tax return for the year.
- Udyam registration (free) done online.
- No office yet, so no trade licence needed (he checked with the panchayat; he works from home and meets clients on site).
- Books: Income and Expenses tabs, invoice numbering RE-2026-001, receipts folder by month; monthly reconciliation on the 1st.
- GST: not needed (turnover far below ₹20 lakh); he notes the threshold in his calendar to review every quarter.

## When you need a licensed professional

- **CA:** structure choice, tax returns and GST.
- **Advocate:** partnership deeds and business agreements.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Agent registration requirements, to plan your documents | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Razorpay: GST on brokerage and commission](https://razorpay.com/learn/gst-on-brokerage-and-commission/) | GST thresholds for services | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [Google Sheets (free with a Google account; works on phones and offline)](https://workspace.google.com/products/sheets/) | Set up the Income and Expenses tabs | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Choose your structure and write why in three lines.
2. Make your set-up checklist with each registration, whether you need it now, and the date you checked (ask your panchayat about trade licences).
3. Open (or designate) a separate bank account for business and set up Income and Expenses tabs with invoice numbering.
4. Enter all income and expenses so far and do your first monthly reconciliation.

**Proof to record:** Your structure choice, the dated set-up checklist, and screenshots of the Income and Expenses tabs (amounts can be blurred).

## Template: Business set-up checklist

```
BUSINESS SET-UP CHECKLIST    checked on ______
Structure: sole proprietor / partnership / LLP / company   Reason: ______
PAN [ ]  Separate bank account [ ]  ITR filed for FY ______ [ ]
Udyam registration [ ] (optional)   Trade licence / Shops and Establishments: needed? Y/N (asked ______ on ______)
K-RERA agent registration: planned by ______ (RE-M10-L01)
GST: turnover this year ₹ ______ ; review on ______ ; register when near ₹20 lakh (CA advice)
Books: Income tab [ ] Expenses tab [ ] invoice numbering [ ] receipts folder [ ] monthly reconciliation date ___
Identity: name ______ email ______ WhatsApp Business [ ] GBP [ ] cards with K-RERA no. and money rules [ ]
```

## Common mistakes

- **Starting a company too early.** Start simple; add structure when needed.
- **Not filing returns.** File every year; you'll need them.
- **Mixing personal and business money.** Separate account and books.

## Local fraud warning

**Fake registration agents.** Some agents charge for "mandatory" registrations that are free (such as Udyam) or not required. Use official portals, ask your CA and check the panchayat's own requirements.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which structure is usually enough for a beginner working alone?
    - A) LLP
    - B) Sole proprietorship
    - C) Trust
    - D) Private limited company
2. Why file income tax returns from year 1?
    - A) They cost nothing to skip
    - B) They are optional forever
    - C) They are needed for K-RERA registration and loans, and build a record
    - D) Only for NRIs
3. When is GST registration required for services?
    - A) From the first rupee
    - B) When turnover exceeds ₹20 lakh a year (or voluntarily)
    - C) Never
    - D) Only for rentals
4. What should you do with clients' money?
    - A) Spend it and repay later
    - B) Use it for expenses
    - C) Mix it in your account
    - D) Keep it separate from yours and record it separately

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the registrations table
- **Action:** choose your structure, make a dated set-up checklist and set up your books. It is done when your proof is saved: your structure choice, the dated set-up checklist, and screenshots of the Income and Expenses tabs (amounts can be blurred).
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **B.** Simplest to start.
2. **C.** Plan ahead.
3. **B.** Check current rules.
4. **D.** Trust and law.

sections.title: RE-M20-L02: Pricing your services, partnerships and growing an agency
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can price your services, set up fair partnerships and co-broking, and plan how to grow from a solo broker into a small agency. **Time:** about 1 hour (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes on pricing and a 12-month plan).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Pricing your services.** Check local practice in your broker interviews, then price to cover your time, travel and risk:
| Service | Common basis | How to agree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sale brokerage | 1% to 2% of price (local practice varies) | Written in the mandate; due on registration |
| Rental brokerage | About one month's rent (sometimes split) | Due on signing |
| NRI property care | Monthly fee per property | Service agreement; monthly invoice |
| Full rental management | Percentage of rent (for example 5% to 10%) | Service agreement |
| Listing and marketing package (for owners or other brokers) | Fixed fee per property (photos, video, copy, posting) | Paid in advance or on delivery |
| Document collection | Fixed fee per task (EC, certificates, tax payment) with written authority | Plus government fees at cost |
Write prices on a simple one-page rate card. Be consistent: discounting heavily for one client undermines trust with others. For pricing method, see the [Entrepreneurship lesson on setting your price](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m05-l03) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course).

**Partnerships and co-broking:**
- **Co-broking with other brokers:** agree in writing who has the mandate, who brings the client, and the split (often 50:50). Tell clients if more than one broker is involved.
- **Referral relationships** with document writers, advocates, engineers, banks and contractors: refer clients to good professionals because they're good. **Don't take or pay secret referral commissions** that clients don't know about; if any referral fee exists, disclose it in writing and make sure it doesn't affect your advice.
- **Partners in your business:** a written agreement (advocate-drafted) covering roles, money, decisions, exit and disputes.

**Growing into an agency:**
1. **Solo (year 1):** rentals, resale, NRI care; build reputation, systems and savings.
2. **Specialise (year 2):** become known for one thing (for example NRI property care in Kuttiady–Nadapuram, or houses for returning Gulf families).
3. **First help:** a part-time assistant for photos and site visits, paid fairly, trained on your checklists and ethics.
4. **Systems:** CRM, checklists, templates, a website or GBP with reviews; written procedures so others can follow them.
5. **Agency:** K-RERA registration for the firm if needed, an office, a few agents, a clear commission split and strict compliance.
Grow only when your systems work and cash flow is steady. See the [Entrepreneurship lesson on hiring, delegating and scaling](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-m12-l03) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course).

**Simple projections.** Estimate deals per month by type × average commission; subtract expenses; compare with your time. Real estate income is uneven: keep 3 to 6 months of expenses as a buffer.

## Local example

**Sachin's rate card and a 12-month plan (illustrative):**
- Rentals: one month's rent from the owner. Sales: 2% from the seller. NRI care: ₹1,500 basic, ₹2,500 standard. Listing package for other brokers: ₹1,500 per property.
- Year 1 target: 2 rentals a month (₹18,000), one sale every two months (avg ₹40,000 → ₹20,000 a month), 5 NRI care clients (₹10,000) = about ₹48,000 a month by month 12, from about ₹8,000 in month 3.
- Expenses: about ₹5,000 a month (phone, travel, portal upgrades).
- Co-broking agreement with the Kakkattil broker: 50:50 split, written.
- Month 9: hire a part-time college student for photo shoots at ₹300 per property.
These are targets, not promises; he reviews them monthly against the CRM.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Business Profile Help: guidelines for service-area businesses](https://support.google.com/business/answer/10514137?hl=en) | Use reviews and service areas to support growth | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Requirements for registering a firm as an agent | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Write your one-page rate card using local practice from your interviews.
2. Draft a co-broking agreement outline and a referral policy (no secret commissions).
3. Build a 12-month plan with monthly targets, expenses and growth steps.
4. Share the rate card with one broker or mentor and note their feedback.

**Proof to record:** The rate card, co-broking outline and referral policy, the 12-month plan and the feedback.

## Template: Rate card and 12-month plan

```
RATE CARD   (name, area, K-RERA no. if registered, money rules)
Sale brokerage ___% (seller) | Rental ___ month's rent | NRI care basic ₹___ standard ₹___ | Full management ___% of rent
Listing package ₹___ | Document collection ₹___ per task + government fees
All payments by bank transfer/UPI with invoice. No cash deals, no undervaluation.
CO-BROKING (written): mandate holder ______ | client introducer ______ | split ___:___ | disclosed to clients Y/N
REFERRAL POLICY: I refer to professionals for quality only; any referral fee is disclosed in writing.
12-MONTH PLAN
Month | Rentals | Sales | NRI clients | Income ₹ | Expenses ₹ | Net ₹ | Growth step
Buffer target: ___ months of expenses
```

## Common mistakes

- **Undercharging to win clients.** Price fairly and consistently.
- **Secret referral commissions.** Disclose any referral fee in writing.
- **Hiring before systems work.** Systems and cash flow first.

## Local fraud warning

**Franchise and "agency in a box" offers.** Some companies sell expensive franchises or leads packages to new brokers with promises of guaranteed deals. Check reviews, ask existing franchisees, and never pay large fees for promises.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What should a co-broking arrangement include?
    - A) Who holds the mandate, who brings the client, and the split, in writing
    - B) The client's salary
    - C) A verbal promise
    - D) Nothing
2. Is it acceptable to take a secret commission from an advocate you refer clients to?
    - A) Only on Sundays
    - B) Yes
    - C) No; any referral fee must be disclosed and must not affect advice
    - D) Yes, if small
3. When should you hire help?
    - A) Never
    - B) Before your first deal
    - C) When systems work and cash flow is steady
    - D) On day 1
4. Why keep a buffer of 3 to 6 months of expenses?
    - A) It is required by law
    - B) Banks demand it
    - C) It is not needed
    - D) Real estate income is uneven

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the pricing table
- **Action:** write your rate card, partnership policies and a 12-month plan. It is done when your proof is saved: the rate card, co-broking outline and referral policy, the 12-month plan and the feedback.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Avoids disputes.
2. **C.** Conflicts of interest.
3. **C.** Grow carefully.
4. **D.** Deals come irregularly.

sections.title: Module 21: Fraud, risk and ethics
sections.summary: Fraud, risk and ethics: the common real estate frauds in Kerala and the checks that catch them, what to do and where to report, a personal code of ethics, conflicts of interest and protecting clients.
sections.content:
*Part C: Run the business.*

## Overview

Read this module early if you can, and keep the red-flag checklist with every deal. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Recognise common frauds and the check for each.
- Know what to do and where to report.
- Apply a code of ethics and handle conflicts.
- Explain risks honestly to clients.

## Time

About 3 hours in total: 2 hours 15 minutes of lessons and 45 minutes for the module project. Part-time: week 15, with the module project due in week 15.

## Lessons

1. RE-M21-L01: Common real estate frauds in Kerala and how to catch them (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M21-L02: Ethics, conflicts of interest and protecting clients (about 1 hour)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- Fraud red-flag checklist (RE-M21-L01).
- Code of ethics and conflict disclosure (RE-M21-L02).

## Module project: a fraud and ethics pack

1. Red-flag checklist and three anonymised local cases.
2. Code of ethics, risk script and conflict disclosure template.
3. Five written responses to difficult situations.
4. Code shown on your card, GBP and mandate.

**Proof to record:** The pack and screenshots.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- Fraud red-flag checklist.
- Code of ethics and conflict disclosure template.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fraud awareness | Generic | Knows the types | Matches local cases to checks |
| Response | Unclear | Knows to stop | Clear steps and reporting routes |
| Ethics | None written | Some rules | Written code used in cards, mandates and practice |
| Conflicts | Ignored | Recognised | Disclosure template and examples |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Memorise the red flags.
- Write your code of ethics.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Main fraud check | Your own EC and certified copies, plus an advocate. |
| POA fraud check | Verify owner directly; check cancellation; pay the owner. |
| Price 30% below market | Red flag. |
| Online payment fraud | Call 1930; report on the national portal. |
| Conflict of interest | Disclose in writing. |
| Licensed work | Drafting, title opinions, surveying, tax advice, valuation certificates. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Thinking "it won't happen to my client".** Use the checklist every time.
- **Silence about problems.** Write them down for the client.
- **Compromising once.** One bad deal can end your reputation.

sections.title: RE-M21-L01: Common real estate frauds in Kerala and how to catch them
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can recognise the common real estate frauds in Kerala, name the check that catches each, and know what to do and where to report if you suspect one. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (20 minutes reading, 40 minutes on the fraud checklist and case review).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

Fraud is the biggest risk for small buyers and sellers, and for your reputation. Almost every fraud is caught by **official records checked by you, an advocate's opinion and patience**.

| Fraud | How it works | The check that catches it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fake or forged title | Forged deeds or certified copies; fake ECs; "lost original" stories | Certified copies and EC from the SRO/PEARL yourself; 30-year chain; advocate |
| Double sale | Same land agreed or sold to two buyers | Fresh EC before agreement and before registration; registered agreement where advised |
| Forged or cancelled POA | Attorney sells an NRI's or elderly owner's land without real authority | Verify the owner directly (video call via advocate); check POA registration and cancellation; pay the owner's account |
| Impersonation | Someone poses as the owner with fake ID | Meet the owner early; compare photos and signatures with earlier deeds; neighbours confirm |
| Heirs left out | One heir sells family land without others | Legal heir certificate; partition deed; all heirs sign |
| Encroachment | Seller includes a neighbour's strip or puramboke; or land is occupied by others | Surveyor measures; sketch and FMB; neighbours; site visits |
| Wrong land type | Nilam or data bank land sold as building land | Tax receipt land type; data bank check; advocate |
| Unapproved layouts | Plots without approval, no proper road, no RERA | Layout approval, K-RERA check, road ownership |
| Undervaluation and black money | Deed shows a low price; rest paid in cash | Refuse; bank payments only; deed shows the true price |
| Advance and deposit scams | Fake landlords or sellers take tokens and vanish | Verify ownership first; pay the owner's account after written agreement |
| Cyber fraud | Fake portals, phishing "EC" links, fake payment screenshots | Official .gov.in sites; confirm payments in the bank app, not screenshots |

**Red flags in behaviour:** pressure to pay today; insistence on cash; refusing an advocate's check; only photocopies; owner "abroad" and unreachable; price far below comparables; changes to documents or people at the last minute; payment to someone other than the owner.

**If you suspect fraud:**
1. **Stop** the deal and any payment. Tell your client calmly and in writing.
2. Send the documents to the client's **advocate**.
3. Keep copies of everything (messages, documents, payment records).
4. For cheating or forgery, the victim can file a complaint with the **police**; for online payment fraud, call **1930** quickly and report on the national portal (cybercrime.gov.in) ([Kerala Police notice](https://ps.keralapolice.gov.in/ernakulamruralcyber-ps/notifications/National-Cyber-Crime-Reporting-Helpline-No-1930-3338)).
5. For project issues (builders), complain to **K-RERA** ([K-RERA](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/)).
Never confront suspected fraudsters alone or try to investigate people yourself beyond checking records; leave that to the police and advocates.

## Local example

A man offers 20 cents near Kuttiady at ₹1.4 lakh per cent (comparables: ₹2 lakh). He says the owner, his uncle in Saudi Arabia, has given him a POA; the original deed is "with the bank"; he wants ₹2 lakh token in cash "today because another buyer is waiting".

Red flags: price 30% below comparables, cash, urgency, absent owner, no original deed. Sachin tells his buyer to pay nothing. The buyer's advocate checks: the POA was registered in 2015, but the EC shows a **cancellation of the POA registered in 2022**. The uncle, reached by video call through the advocate, confirms he had cancelled it and is not selling. The buyer is saved ₹2 lakh, and the uncle is warned that someone is trying to sell his land.

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** any suspected fraud, before any further step.
- **Police:** cheating, forgery, impersonation.
- **Licensed surveyor:** encroachment and boundary questions.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Police notice: National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline 1930 and the portal cybercrime.gov.in](https://ps.keralapolice.gov.in/ernakulamruralcyber-ps/notifications/National-Cyber-Crime-Reporting-Helpline-No-1930-3338) | Read about the 1930 helpline and the national portal | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Housing.com (April 2025): how to get an encumbrance certificate in Kerala](https://housing.com/news/steps-to-get-an-encumbrance-certificate-in-kerala/amp) | EC steps (your main fraud check) | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |
| [TaxGuru (15 October 2011): Supreme Court in Suraj Lamp & Industries v. State of Haryana, GPA sales do not transfer title](https://taxguru.in/corporate-law/general-power-attorney-legal-sanctity-immovable-property-sold-transferred-registered-deeds-sc.html) | Why POA sales don't transfer title | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Ask two brokers and your document writer or advocate about real fraud cases they have seen in your area (no names), and how each was or could have been caught.
2. Match each case to a row in the fraud table.
3. Build your fraud red-flag checklist and add it to your due-diligence file.
4. Save the 1930 helpline and the police station number in your phone and on your toolkit.

**Proof to record:** Notes on at least three local fraud cases (anonymised), your red-flag checklist and saved contacts.

## Template: Fraud red-flag checklist

```
FRAUD RED-FLAG CHECKLIST (any YES -> stop and call the advocate)
[ ] Price far below comparables (>20%)        [ ] Pressure to pay today
[ ] Cash demanded or "part in cash"           [ ] Only photocopies; original "lost" or "with someone"
[ ] Owner absent and unreachable; POA seller  [ ] Payment to someone other than the owner
[ ] Names/areas/survey numbers don't match     [ ] Heirs or co-owners missing
[ ] Land type nilam / data bank / puramboke    [ ] No layout approval or RERA number (projects)
[ ] Documents or people change at the last minute  [ ] Seller refuses advocate's check or fresh EC
IF FRAUD SUSPECTED: stop payments -> tell client in writing -> advocate -> keep records -> police / 1930 (online payment fraud) / K-RERA (projects)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Ignoring red flags because the deal looks good.** Below-market prices are the most common bait.
- **Investigating suspects yourself.** Check records; leave investigation to police and advocates.
- **Delaying reports of payment fraud.** Call 1930 quickly.

## Local fraud warning

**Fraud against the broker.** Fraudsters also use brokers to look legitimate. Protect yourself: verify every owner before listing, never collect money for owners, and keep written records of what you checked and told clients.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What catches most double sales?
    - A) A cash token
    - B) Trusting the seller
    - C) A fresh EC before the agreement and before registration
    - D) A nice brochure
2. A seller with a POA wants a cash token today. You:
    - A) Pay quickly
    - B) Ignore the POA
    - C) Advise the client to pay nothing until the advocate verifies the owner and POA
    - D) Pay half
3. Where do you report online payment fraud quickly?
    - A) Nowhere
    - B) Helpline 1930 and the national cybercrime portal
    - C) The seller
    - D) A WhatsApp group
4. How do you avoid buying nilam sold as building land?
    - A) Ask the seller
    - B) Look at the soil
    - C) Trust the broker
    - D) Check the land type in revenue records and the data bank

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the fraud table
- **Action:** collect three anonymised local fraud cases and build your red-flag checklist. It is done when your proof is saved: notes on at least three local fraud cases (anonymised), your red-flag checklist and saved contacts.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** It shows registered transactions.
2. **C.** Several red flags.
3. **B.** Speed helps recovery.
4. **D.** Records, not appearances.

sections.title: RE-M21-L02: Ethics, conflicts of interest and protecting clients
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can apply a clear code of ethics, handle conflicts of interest and protect clients, and explain why honest dealing is also good business. **Time:** about 1 hour (15 minutes reading, 45 minutes on your code and case responses).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Your code of ethics:**
| Principle | In practice |
| --- | --- |
| Consent | Market only with the owner's written mandate; share details only with consent |
| Truth | Never misrepresent a property, its papers, its risks or your own role |
| Money | No cash beyond legal limits, no undervaluation, no black money, no benami |
| Loyalty and fairness | Act for your client; deal honestly with the other side; disclose if you are paid by both |
| Conflicts | Disclose any personal interest (your family's property, your own purchase, referral fees) |
| Limits | Never do work that needs a licence you don't have (drafting, title opinions, surveying, tax advice, valuation certificates) |
| Privacy | Protect documents and personal data; delete what you no longer need |
| Compliance | Follow K-RERA rules, register when required, keep records |

**Conflicts of interest.** A conflict exists when your interest could pull against your client's.
- **Buying for yourself** a property you were asked to sell: tell the owner in writing, suggest they get an independent opinion on price, or step back.
- **Selling your family's property** to your client: disclose it.
- **Taking commission from both sides:** disclose it to both in writing (RE-M10-L02).
- **Referral fees** from advocates, banks or contractors: disclose them, or better, don't take them (RE-M20-L02).
- **Pushing a property because the commission is higher:** don't; show what fits the client.

**Protecting clients:**
- Encourage every buyer to use their own advocate and, where needed, a surveyor.
- Keep tokens small and conditional; payments to the owner's account by bank transfer.
- Put important information in writing (WhatsApp or email): issues found, advice to get an advocate, offers.
- Tell clients the honest risks: illiquidity, legal disputes, market downturns and low yields (Module 18).
- Know when to walk away and say so.

**Why ethics is good business.** In a small market like Kuttiady, reputation travels fast. One dishonest deal can end a career; ten honest deals bring a stream of referrals. NRI clients, in particular, choose agents they can trust from thousands of kilometres away.

**Honest risk talk (a script):** "Property can be a good home and sometimes a good investment, but it's hard to sell quickly, legal problems can take years to solve, prices don't always rise, and after costs many small purchases earn less than a fixed deposit. Let's check the numbers and get an advocate's opinion before you decide."

## Local example

**Three situations and Sachin's responses:**
1. An owner asks him to advertise a plot as "10 cents" when the deed says 8.6: he refuses and lists 8.6 cents, explaining that misrepresentation will kill the deal at the advocate stage anyway.
2. A buyer from Dubai asks him to "manage everything, including signing for me": he explains he can coordinate, but legal acts need a registered POA in favour of someone the buyer trusts, and the buyer's own advocate.
3. He finds a plot he wants to buy himself, listed with him by an elderly owner: he tells the owner in writing, recommends she get a second broker's or valuer's view on price, and offers the comparables price, not a lower one. She agrees, and both sides use their own advocates.

## When you need a licensed professional

- **Advocate:** for any conflict you are unsure about, and for clients who need legal acts done.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Look for any code of conduct or obligations for agents on the K-RERA site | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Wikipedia: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Estate_%28Regulation_and_Development%29_Act,_2016) | Re-read the agents' obligations under RERA | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Write your own code of ethics (8 principles, one line each) and your honest risk script.
2. Write how you would respond to five difficult situations (the three above plus two from your interviews).
3. Add your code to your website or GBP description, visiting card and mandate (short version).
4. Ask one mentor, broker or advocate to read your code and suggest one improvement.

**Proof to record:** Your code, risk script, five written responses and the feedback.

## Template: Code of ethics and conflict disclosure

```
MY CODE OF ETHICS (short version for cards and profiles)
I act only with owners' written consent. I never misrepresent a property. All payments go by bank transfer
to the right person; no cash deals, no undervaluation. I disclose any personal interest or fee.
I don't do work that needs a licence I don't hold; I bring in advocates, surveyors and CAs.
I protect your documents and privacy.
CONFLICT DISCLOSURE (to client, in writing)
"I want to tell you that ______ (my relative owns this property / I am also paid by the other side / I would like to buy this myself / I receive a referral fee from ______). You may want an independent opinion. Please confirm you are happy for me to continue." Date ______ Client's reply ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Hiding a personal interest.** Disclose in writing.
- **Doing licensed work to save the client money.** Refer to professionals.
- **Avoiding uncomfortable truths.** Use your honest risk script.

## Local fraud warning

**"Everyone does it."** Undervaluation, cash and hidden commissions are common, which makes them feel normal. They are still illegal or dishonest, and they expose you to penalties and lost trust. Your clean record is your competitive advantage.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. You want to buy a property an owner asked you to sell. What do you do?
    - A) Buy it secretly at a low price
    - B) Raise your commission
    - C) Disclose in writing and suggest an independent price opinion
    - D) Tell nobody
2. A client asks you to sign documents for them. You:
    - A) Ask a friend to sign
    - B) Forge their signature
    - C) Sign anyway
    - D) Explain that legal acts need a registered POA and their own advocate
3. Why is ethics good business in a small market?
    - A) Because of taxes
    - B) It isn't
    - C) Reputation travels fast and referrals depend on trust
    - D) Only for NRIs
4. Which work needs a licence you don't have?
    - A) Drafting deeds, title opinions, surveying, tax advice and valuation certificates
    - B) Taking photos
    - C) Running site visits
    - D) Writing listings

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the ethics table
- **Action:** write your code of ethics, risk script and responses to five difficult situations. It is done when your proof is saved: your code, risk script, five written responses and the feedback.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** Conflict of interest.
2. **D.** Know your limits.
3. **C.** Trust is the product.
4. **A.** Refer to professionals.

Action: write your code of ethics, risk script and responses to five difficult situations
tasks.detail: **Proof to record:** Your code, risk script, five written responses and the feedback. Save it in your Real Estate Toolkit folder (21 Fraud, risk and ethics) and note where it is.

sections.title: Module 22: Capstone: your first deal or your business plan
sections.summary: The capstone: close a first real deal legally (a rental or a sale) with proper written agreements, **or** complete a full investment analysis and a business plan, together with your complete Real Estate Toolkit. Then retake the quiz and plan the next 12 months.
sections.content:
*Part C: Run the business.*

## Overview

Both options use the same standards: written consent, honest marketing, professionals for licensed work, bank payments only and no black money. A deal that stops honestly at a problem is still a pass. Everything is as of November 2026; check current rules.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Plan and run a five-week capstone.
- Close a first deal legally, or produce a full analysis and business plan.
- Assemble and test the complete toolkit.
- Measure progress and plan the next 12 months.

## Time

About 13 hours 45 minutes in total: 12 hours 45 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 16–21, with the module project due in week 21.

## Lessons

1. RE-M22-L01: Choose your capstone and plan it (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
2. RE-M22-L02: Run the capstone (about 10 hours)
3. RE-M22-L03: Final retest, your toolkit and the next 12 months (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Copy-ready tools in this module

- Capstone plan (RE-M22-L01).
- Capstone weekly log and review (RE-M22-L02).
- Toolkit index and 12-month plan (RE-M22-L03).

## Module project: your capstone: first deal or analysis + business plan, plus the full toolkit

1. Choose and plan (RE-M22-L01).
2. Run it for five weeks with logs (RE-M22-L02).
3. Assemble the toolkit, retest and plan (RE-M22-L03).
4. Optional: show your deal file or plan to a broker or advocate you interviewed and note their feedback.

**Proof to record:** The deal file or analysis and plan, five logs, the review, the toolkit index and the retest comparison.

## Add to your Real Estate Toolkit

Save these in your toolkit folder and Google Sheets workbook (set up in Week 0). By the capstone they form your complete business toolkit.

- The complete toolkit folder with index.
- Your deal file or analysis and business plan.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legal and ethical | Cash, no consent or licensed work done by you | Mostly compliant | Written consent, agreements, bank payments, professionals at every step |
| Completeness | Missing key documents | Most documents | Every checklist and record in the file |
| Numbers | Guesses | Some calculations | Dated rates, full costs and returns with a downside case |
| Reflection | None | Brief | Honest review with problems, fixes and next steps |
| Toolkit | Scattered | Mostly gathered | Complete, tested in Sheets and LibreOffice, dated |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, for weeks when PSC study or work leaves little time:

- Do Option B on one property and a one-page plan.
- Assemble the core 15 tools.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, say the answer aloud, then check.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Capstone options | A: first real deal; B: analysis + business plan. |
| Most realistic first deal | A rental. |
| If the deal stalls | Submit up to the furthest stage plus a plan. |
| Capstone time | 10 hours over five weeks. |
| Toolkit rule | Every rate dated; "check current rules". |
| Quarterly habit | Re-check rules on official sources. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Cutting corners to finish.** Standards over speed.
- **No records.** The file is your proof.
- **Stopping after the course.** Follow your 12-month plan.

sections.title: RE-M22-L01: Choose your capstone and plan it
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can choose the right capstone (a first real deal, or a complete investment analysis plus business plan), set a realistic five-week plan and prepare every document and tool you will need. **Time:** about 1 hour 15 minutes (20 minutes reading, 55 minutes planning).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

The capstone brings the whole course together. Choose **one** option:
| Option | What you do | Choose it if |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. First real deal | Close a real rental or sale legally, with a signed mandate, proper written agreements, bank payments and the full checklists | You have at least one mandated property or a serious client, and an advocate or document writer you can work with |
| B. Investment analysis + business plan | A complete analysis of a real property (due diligence on public and permitted information, valuation, full costs, returns, risks) plus a 12-month business plan, with everything ready for a first deal | No deal is ready yet, or you are short on time |

Both options require the **full toolkit** (RE-M22-L03) and the same legal and ethical standards: owner's written consent, honest marketing, advocates for title opinions, licensed professionals for licensed work, bank payments only and no black money.

**Option A: first real deal.** A rental is the most realistic first deal (smaller amounts, faster, fewer legal steps). A sale is fine if you already have a mandate and a serious buyer. Your deal file must include: mandate; listing with approval; CRM records; intake and site-visit checklists; due-diligence checklist (for a sale) or tenant screening (for a rental); token receipt or deposit record (bank transfer); agreement (prepared or reviewed by an advocate or document writer); for a sale, the transaction timeline to registration and handover; invoice and payment record.
**If the deal doesn't close in five weeks** (common: deals take time), submit everything up to the furthest stage reached, plus Option B's business plan. That still counts.

**Option B: investment analysis + business plan.** Choose a real property you can analyse with permission or from public information (or the course's sample case for the legal part): comparables valuation, fair value check, full cost of purchase, rental yield and returns with a downside case, due-diligence checklist with the issues you'd send to an advocate, and a recommendation **framework** (not a recommendation to buy). Add a 12-month business plan: services, rate card, sourcing, marketing, monthly targets, compliance (K-RERA, GST, books) and risks.

**Planning:** list every step, who is involved, what document is needed and a target week. Book time with professionals early. Your weekly schedule stays at 5 to 7 hours (10 hours of capstone work spread over five weeks).

## Local example

Sachin chooses **Option A (rental)**: a 2-bedroom house in Kakkattil whose owner (an NRI in Muscat) has signed a mandate. His five-week plan:
- Week 1: photos, video, bilingual listing approved by the owner; posted on two portals, WhatsApp Business and Facebook Marketplace.
- Week 2: enquiries into the CRM; intake calls; three site visits.
- Week 3: screening of two applicants; the owner chooses; police station guidance followed.
- Week 4: advocate-reviewed agreement; stamp paper; deposit and first rent by bank transfer to the owner; inventory and meter photos.
- Week 5: handover; invoice for one month's rent to the owner; review and testimonial request.
Backup: if it doesn't close, he completes Option B on a 10-cent plot in his market study.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Check whether your deal needs K-RERA registration (project units do) | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [India Code: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 (PDF)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20372/1/kerala_buildings_lease_and_rent_ctrl_act_1965.pdf) | Rental rules if you choose a rental | 10 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Square Yards (updated July 2026): stamp duty and registration charges in Kerala](https://www.squareyards.com/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-kerala) | Current stamp duty for the deal type | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 through a secondary source; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Choose Option A or B and write why in three lines.
2. Write a five-week plan with steps, people, documents and target weeks.
3. List the professionals you'll need and contact them now.
4. Prepare your deal file folders from the transaction file template.

**Proof to record:** Your choice, the five-week plan, the professionals list and the empty (ready) deal file.

## Template: Capstone plan

```
CAPSTONE PLAN          Option: A (first deal: rental / sale) / B (analysis + business plan)
Why this option: ______
Week | Steps | People involved | Documents needed | Done
1 | ______ | ______ | ______ | [ ]
2 | ______ | ______ | ______ | [ ]
3 | ______ | ______ | ______ | [ ]
4 | ______ | ______ | ______ | [ ]
5 | ______ | ______ | ______ | [ ]
Professionals: advocate ______ document writer ______ surveyor (if needed) ______ CA (if needed) ______
Legal and ethics check: mandate [ ] honest listing [ ] bank payments only [ ] advocate for title [ ] no licensed work by me [ ]
Backup if the deal stalls: ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Choosing a big sale as the first deal.** A rental is the realistic first deal.
- **No backup plan.** Option B is the fallback.
- **Booking professionals late.** Contact them in week 1.

## Local fraud warning

**Rushing to finish the course.** Don't let a deadline make you cut corners: no cash, no skipped checks, no listing without consent. A capstone that stops at an honest "the title had a problem" is a pass.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which first deal is usually most realistic?
    - A) A rental
    - B) A builder's whole project
    - C) A flip with a loan
    - D) A large plotting project
2. What if the deal doesn't close in five weeks?
    - A) Close it with cash
    - B) Submit everything up to the furthest stage plus the business plan
    - C) Skip the checks
    - D) Fail the course
3. What does Option B NOT include?
    - A) Valuation
    - B) A business plan
    - C) A recommendation to buy a specific property
    - D) Full costs and returns
4. When should you contact professionals for the capstone?
    - A) In week 1
    - B) On the last day
    - C) Never
    - D) After registration

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and the two options
- **Action:** choose your capstone and write a five-week plan. It is done when your proof is saved: your choice, the five-week plan, the professionals list and the empty (ready) deal file.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Smaller and faster.
2. **B.** Honest progress counts.
3. **C.** No investment recommendations.
4. **A.** They need time.

sections.title: RE-M22-L02: Run the capstone
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can carry out your capstone over five weeks, keeping every document, payment and decision legal, written and recorded. **Time:** about 10 hours (10 hours over five weeks (about 2 hours a week, inside your 5 to 7 hour schedule)).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**Weekly rhythm (about 2 hours of capstone work):**
1. Monday: review the plan; update the CRM and deal file.
2. During the week: do the steps (visits, calls, documents).
3. Sunday: weekly log, write what happened, what's blocked and next week's three actions.

**Option A checklist (first deal):**
- [ ] Signed mandate (RE-M10-L02) and owner-approved photos and listing (RE-M12).
- [ ] Listing live on free portals and social channels; every enquiry in the CRM (RE-M19-L01).
- [ ] Intake and site-visit checklists for each visit (RE-M13-L01).
- [ ] **Rental:** tenant screening (RE-M15-L01), advocate-reviewed agreement, correct stamp paper, deposit and rent by bank transfer to the owner, inventory and meter readings, verification as required locally.
- [ ] **Sale:** due-diligence checklist and the buyer's advocate's opinion (RE-M06), conditional token by bank transfer (RE-M13-L02), agreement for sale by an advocate or document writer, cost calculation with current rates, TDS if applicable, registration, mutation and handover (RE-M14).
- [ ] Invoice and commission by bank transfer; Income tab updated (RE-M09-L02).
- [ ] A short deal review: what went well, what you'd change, the client's feedback.

**Option B checklist (analysis + business plan):**
- [ ] Property chosen with permission or from public information; sample case for the legal checks if needed.
- [ ] Comparables (from your 20+ listings) and fair value check (RE-M07).
- [ ] Full cost of purchase with current dated rates (RE-M08-L02).
- [ ] Yield, cash-on-cash and 5-year IRR with a downside case (RE-M08-L02, RE-M18-L01).
- [ ] Due-diligence checklist with issues for an advocate (RE-M06-L03).
- [ ] Risk section: liquidity, legal and market (RE-M18).
- [ ] 12-month business plan: services, rate card, sourcing, marketing, monthly targets, compliance and risks (RE-M20).
- [ ] Ready-for-first-deal pack: mandate, listing, intake, site-visit, token and rental templates printed or saved.

**When something goes wrong** (it often does): a missing heir, a refusing bank, a tenant who backs out. Stop, write it down, get the right professional's advice and decide with the client. Record it in the deal review: handling problems properly is the real skill.

## Local example

Sachin's rental capstone, week by week (summary from his log):
- Week 1: listing live (NoBroker, Facebook Marketplace, WhatsApp Business); 7 enquiries.
- Week 2: 4 intake calls, 3 visits; one couple very interested.
- Week 3: screening done; the owner (by video call) chooses the couple; Sachin asks the local police station about verification and follows its advice.
- Week 4: advocate-reviewed agreement on the right stamp paper; deposit and first month's rent paid by bank transfer to the owner; inventory and meter photos signed.
- Week 5: keys handed over; ₹9,000 invoice to the owner, paid by bank transfer; review on his Google Business Profile.
Deal review: the slowest step was getting the owner's signature from abroad (solved by a scanned signed copy followed by the original by courier, as the advocate advised). Next time: arrange signing logistics in week 1.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Project rules if relevant | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Income Tax Department: TDS on the sum paid to buy an immovable property](https://incometaxindia.gov.in/w/tds-from-sum-paid-to-buy-an-immovable-property) | TDS if a sale is ₹50 lakh or more | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |
| [Ente Bhoomi: Kerala integrated land information portal](https://entebhoomi.kerala.gov.in/) | Mutation check after a sale | 5 minutes | unverified: the site blocks automated checks; type the address yourself |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Follow your five-week plan, with a weekly log entry every Sunday.
2. Keep every document, message and payment record in the deal file.
3. Tick the checklist for your option as you go.
4. At the end, write a one-page deal (or analysis) review.

**Proof to record:** The complete deal file (or analysis and business plan), five weekly log entries and the one-page review (private details masked in anything shared).

## Template: Capstone weekly log and review

```
CAPSTONE WEEKLY LOG   Week ___ of 5
Done this week: ______
Blocked / problems: ______ ; professional consulted: ______
Documents added to the file: ______
Next week's three actions: 1 ______ 2 ______ 3 ______
FINAL REVIEW (one page)
Option and outcome: ______
What went well: ______   What went wrong and how I handled it: ______
Legal and ethics check passed? mandate | consent | written agreements | bank payments | professionals used  Y/N each
Client feedback: ______
What I will do differently in my next deal: ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Missing weekly logs.** Write every Sunday; it is your evidence.
- **Doing a professional's job to save time.** Use the right professional every time.
- **Hiding problems in the review.** Problems handled well are the best evidence of skill.

## Local fraud warning

**Late surprises.** Even in a small rental, a "landlord" may turn out not to be the owner, or a tenant may give fake ID. Your checks protect your first deal as much as your hundredth.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How much capstone work is planned each week?
    - A) None
    - B) 20 hours
    - C) About 2 hours inside your 5 to 7 hour schedule
    - D) 10 hours a day
2. A rental deposit should be paid:
    - A) By bank transfer to the owner, with the agreement signed
    - B) In cash to you
    - C) In cash to the owner
    - D) Before the visit
3. Something goes wrong in week 3. What do you do?
    - A) Stop, record it, get the right professional's advice and decide with the client
    - B) Cut corners
    - C) Hide it
    - D) Abandon the client
4. What is the proof for the capstone?
    - A) A friend's opinion
    - B) A screenshot of the course
    - C) The deal file or analysis and plan, five weekly logs and a review
    - D) Nothing

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and your option's checklist
- **Action:** run your capstone for five weeks with weekly logs and a final review. It is done when your proof is saved: the complete deal file (or analysis and business plan), five weekly log entries and the one-page review (private details masked in anything shared).
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **C.** 10 hours over five weeks.
2. **A.** Your money rules.
3. **A.** Handling problems is the skill.
4. **C.** Evidence of real work.
