sections.title: RE-M22-L03: Final retest, your toolkit and the next 12 months
sections.summary: **Outcome:** You can assemble your complete Real Estate Toolkit, retake the knowledge quiz to measure progress and set your plan for the next 12 months. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (15 minutes reading, 75 minutes assembling the toolkit and planning (the final retest is on its own page)).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

**1. Assemble your toolkit.** Gather every template and calculator into one folder (and a printed set for site visits). The core items are listed below; the full text of each is on the [Toolkit page](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/kerala-real-estate/re-toolkit):
| Tool | Where you learned it |
| --- | --- |
| Comparables sheet with formulas | RE-M07-L01 |
| Full cost of a purchase | RE-M04-L01 and RE-M14-L02 |
| Rental yield and return calculator | RE-M08-L02 |
| EMI formulas | RE-M08-L01 |
| Due-diligence checklist | RE-M06-L03 |
| Document checklist by deal type | RE-M05-L04 |
| Owner mandate template | RE-M10-L02 |
| Client intake form | RE-M13-L01 |
| Site-visit checklist | RE-M13-L01 |
| Listing template | RE-M12-L02 |
| CRM sheet | RE-M19-L01 |
| Transaction timeline | RE-M14-L01 |
| Rental agreement checklist | RE-M05-L03 and RE-M15-L01 |
| NRI property care service menu | RE-M15-L02 |
| Weekly market log | Week 1 onwards |
Also include what you built in the modules: the land records comparison, portal guide, legal red-flag checklist, deed reading sheet, title chain and EC sheet, valuation sheets, loan calculator, tax questions, mandate and inventory, interview guide, network tab, photo checklist, token receipt, transaction file, screening form, service menu and monthly report, plotting and construction sheets, strategy and REIT sheets, AI rules, set-up checklist, rate card, fraud red flags and code of ethics.
Check every formula works in both Google Sheets and LibreOffice. Date-stamp every rate (stamp duty, fees, thresholds) and add a "check current rules" note.

**2. Retake the quiz.** Go to the [Final retest page](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/kerala-real-estate/re-final): take knowledge quiz form B, compare with your baseline, and re-rate your skills.

**3. Plan the next 12 months.** Use the [What next page](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/kerala-real-estate/re-next). A realistic path:
- **Months 1 to 3:** 2 to 4 rentals, 2 NRI care clients, keep your market study current.
- **Months 4 to 6:** first sale (co-broke if needed); file your return; decide on K-RERA registration.
- **Months 7 to 12:** specialise (for example NRI property care or houses for returning families); build reviews and referrals; consider an assistant.
- **Every quarter:** re-check rates and rules on official sources (stamp duty, fair value, K-RERA, GST, tax) and update your toolkit.
- **Investing:** only after steady service income, an emergency fund and a full analysis (Module 18).

**4. Keep learning:** the Entrepreneurship, Social Media Marketing and Personal Finance courses in this app; the [MIT real estate finance course](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/11-431j-real-estate-finance-and-investment-fall-2006) for deeper finance; and the people you met: brokers, document writers and advocates are your best teachers.

## Local example

Sachin's toolkit folder: 15 core templates plus 22 module tools, all dated "rates as of November 2026; check current rules". His retest: knowledge score from 4/12 to 11/12; skills self-rating from 14/50 to 38/50. His 12-month plan targets 30 rentals, 3 sales and 8 NRI care clients, K-RERA registration in month 6, and a quarterly rules check on the first Sunday of January, April, July and October.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Sheets (free with a Google account; works on phones and offline)](https://workspace.google.com/products/sheets/) | Check every formula in Sheets | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [LibreOffice (free and open source; Calc spreadsheet works on an old laptop)](https://www.libreoffice.org/) | Check every formula in Calc | 15 minutes | verified 2026-11-04 |
| [Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA): agent and project registration, complaints, project search](https://rera.kerala.gov.in/) | Re-check agent registration before your plan | 5 minutes | verified 2026-11-04; check current rules |

## Action task (in your local market)

1. Assemble the full toolkit folder and test every formula in Sheets and LibreOffice.
2. Date-stamp every rate and add "check current rules".
3. Take the final retest and compare with your baseline.
4. Write your 12-month plan with quarterly rules checks.

**Proof to record:** The toolkit folder index, the tested formulas, your retest comparison and your 12-month plan.

## Template: Toolkit index and 12-month plan

```
TOOLKIT INDEX    rates as of ______; check current rules
Core: Comps | Cost | ROI | EMI | Due diligence | Document checklist | Mandate | Intake | Site visit | Listing | CRM | Timeline | Rental agreement | NRI care | Weekly log
Module tools: ______ (list)
Formula test: Sheets [ ] LibreOffice [ ]
12-MONTH PLAN
Quarter | Rentals | Sales | NRI clients | Learning | Compliance (K-RERA / ITR / GST / rules check) | Income target
Q1 | ___ | ___ | ___ | ______ | rules check on ______ | ₹ ___
Q2 | ...
Q3 | ...
Q4 | ...
```

## Common mistakes

- **Letting the toolkit go stale.** Quarterly rules check.
- **Skipping the retest.** It shows your progress and gaps.
- **A plan without numbers.** Set targets you can track in the CRM.

## Local fraud warning

**Outdated rules as a risk.** Stamp duty, fair values, tax sections, thresholds and portals change. Using an old rate can cost a client money or break the law. Your quarterly check is part of protecting clients.

## Quiz

Answer from memory first. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How often should you re-check rates and rules?
    - A) Every quarter, and before every deal
    - B) Only when a client complains
    - C) Every 10 years
    - D) Never
2. What should every rate in your toolkit carry?
    - A) A date and a "check current rules" note
    - B) Nothing
    - C) A guarantee
    - D) The broker's signature
3. When should you consider investing in property yourself?
    - A) After steady service income, an emergency fund and a full analysis
    - B) Never think about it
    - C) With borrowed money first
    - D) Right now
4. Where do you take the final knowledge retest?
    - A) The glossary
    - B) The Final retest page
    - C) The start page
    - D) Nowhere

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** read the lesson and gather your module tools
- **Action:** assemble and test the full toolkit, take the retest and write your 12-month plan. It is done when your proof is saved: the toolkit folder index, the tested formulas, your retest comparison and your 12-month plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the lesson and try again tomorrow.

## Answers

1. **A.** Rules change.
2. **A.** Shows when it was verified.
3. **A.** Services first.
4. **B.** Form B compares with the baseline.

sections.title: Final retest and checklist
sections.summary: Quiz form B, skills rating, comparison with your baseline and the final checklist of your real estate toolkit.
sections.content:
Take **form B** of the quiz and the skills rating, compare them with your baseline, and tick the final checklist.

## Knowledge quiz, form B (12 questions, 15 minutes)

Answer without looking anything up; guessing is fine. Score 1 per correct answer, out of 12. Cover the answers first.

1. A plot is 10 cents. About how many square feet is that?
    - A) About 1,000 sq ft
    - B) About 43,560 sq ft
    - C) About 4,356 sq ft
    - D) About 435 sq ft
2. A deed says 4.05 ares. About how many cents is that?
    - A) About 40 cents
    - B) About 10 cents
    - C) About 1 cent
    - D) About 4 cents
3. What does the thandaper (thandaper number) record?
    - A) The building permit number
    - B) The bank loan number
    - C) The sale price
    - D) The landholder's account in the village revenue records, used for land tax
4. An EC for 13 years shows no entries. What can you safely conclude?
    - A) The title is perfect
    - B) Only that no registered transactions appear for those 13 years; older history and unregistered claims still need checking
    - C) The land is not paddy land
    - D) There are no court cases
5. A sale deed must be presented for registration within how long of signing?
    - A) Within one week
    - B) Within ten years
    - C) There is no time limit
    - D) Within four months
6. Price Rs 30 lakh; fair value Rs 34 lakh. On what value is stamp duty calculated?
    - A) Rs 30 lakh
    - B) Rs 34 lakh, the higher of the two
    - C) Rs 4 lakh, the difference
    - D) Rs 32 lakh, the average
7. What can a real estate agent registered with K-RERA NOT do?
    - A) Arrange site visits
    - B) Collect commission by bank transfer with an invoice
    - C) Give a legal title opinion or draft and register deeds without the required licence
    - D) Market a property with the owner's mandate
8. Building near the coast may need clearance under which rules?
    - A) Rent control law
    - B) Benami law
    - C) Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) rules
    - D) RERA agent rules
9. Net operating income is Rs 1.2 lakh a year on a Rs 30 lakh property. What is the cap rate?
    - A) 12%
    - B) 40%
    - C) 4%
    - D) 0.4%
10. GST on the resale of a completed house with an occupancy certificate is:
    - A) 18%
    - B) 12%
    - C) Not charged
    - D) 5% always
11. Which step comes right after registration of a sale deed?
    - A) Mutation of the land records (pokkuvaravu) into the buyer's name
    - B) Paying the token advance
    - C) Signing the agreement for sale
    - D) Applying for an EC for the next 30 years
12. A layout of plots is sold with "approval coming soon". What is the main risk?
    - A) Unapproved layouts may not get building permits, roads or utilities, and buyers can lose money
    - B) No risk if the land is cheap
    - C) Prices always rise
    - D) Banks prefer unapproved layouts

### Answers, form B

1. **C.** 10 × 435.6 = 4,356 sq ft (RE-M03-L01).
2. **B.** 4.05 × 2.47 ≈ 10 cents (RE-M03-L01).
3. **D.** It links the owner to land-tax records (RE-M03-L02).
4. **B.** Search 30+ years and check other sources (RE-M06-L01).
5. **D.** Section 23 of the Registration Act (RE-M04-L01).
6. **B.** Duty is on the higher of price or fair value (RE-M04-L01).
7. **C.** Legal work needs an advocate; deeds need a licensed document writer or advocate (RE-M10-L01).
8. **C.** CRZ 2019 and Kerala's approved coastal plan (RE-M04-L04).
9. **C.** 1.2 ÷ 30 = 4% (RE-M08-L02).
10. **C.** GST applies to under-construction property, not resale (RE-M09-L02).
11. **A.** Mutation updates revenue records (RE-M14-L03).
12. **A.** Unapproved layouts are a common trap (RE-M16-L01, RE-M21-L01).

## Skills self-rating (5 minutes)

| No | Statement (rate 1 = not at all, 5 = fully) | Start | End |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | I can explain the steps of a property sale from token advance to mutation. |  |  |
| 2 | I can read a sale deed and an EC and point out what to check. |  |  |
| 3 | I can convert cents, ares and square feet without a calculator app. |  |  |
| 4 | I can find a property's fair value on the official portal. |  |  |
| 5 | I can calculate the full cost of buying a property. |  |  |
| 6 | I can calculate rental yield and cap rate. |  |  |
| 7 | I know which tasks need an advocate, a surveyor, a CA or a document writer. |  |  |
| 8 | I can write an honest listing and market it for free. |  |  |
| 9 | I know at least five local brokers or property professionals. |  |  |
| 10 | I can spot at least five common real estate frauds. |  |  |

Add the scores (10 to 50).

## Compare

| Measure | Start | End | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Knowledge quiz (out of 12) |  |  |  |
| Skills self-rating (10–50) |  |  |  |
| Listings in your Comps sheet | 0 |  |  |
| Property professionals you know |  |  |  |
| Leads in your CRM | 0 |  |  |

## Final checklist

| Item | Built in |
| --- | --- |
| Comparables sheet with 20+ local listings and price per cent / per sq ft | RE-M07-L03 |
| Fair value compared with market prices for at least 3 properties | RE-M07-L01 |
| Interview notes from 3 brokers and 1 document writer or advocate | RE-M11-L01 |
| Annotated sale deed, EC and rental agreement samples | Module 5 |
| A completed due-diligence checklist on a real or sample property | RE-M06-L03 |
| A full purchase cost calculation using current official rates | RE-M04-L01 |
| ROI analysis for 5 real properties | RE-M08-L02 |
| A real listing with the owner's written permission, live on free portals and social media | Module 12 |
| CRM sheet with every lead tracked | RE-M19-L01 |
| A real site visit conducted or shadowed | RE-M13-L01 |
| All toolkit templates adapted to your area | Toolkit page |
| Capstone: a first legal deal with written agreements, or an investment analysis plus business plan | Module 22 |

sections.title: What next: your 12-month roadmap
sections.summary: A 12-month plan to grow from first deals to a small agency or specialist service, with free resources to go deeper.
sections.content:
## The next 12 months

| When | Focus | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | Get to 10 active mandates or rental listings | Weekly market log, owner outreach, honest listings |
| Months 1–3 | Register with K-RERA if your work requires it | RE-M10-L01; check current rules |
| Months 3–6 | Close 2–4 rentals and 1 sale, or sign 3 NRI care clients | Written mandates, transaction timeline, CRM |
| Months 6–9 | Build referral partners: an advocate, a surveyor, a CA, a document writer, two banks | RE-M11 and RE-M14 |
| Months 9–12 | Decide: grow a small agency, specialise (NRI, rentals, land), or start a small investment | RE-M18 and RE-M20; keep an emergency fund first |
| Every month | Update comparables and check one rule on an official source | Weekly market log |

## Go deeper (free)

- [MIT OCW Real Estate Finance and Investment](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/11-431j-real-estate-finance-and-investment-fall-2006): lecture notes and problem sets (about 2 hours per topic).
- [OpenStax Principles of Finance](https://openstax.org/books/principles-finance/pages/preface): chapters 7–9 on time value of money (about 2 hours each).
- Other courses in this app: [Practical Entrepreneurship](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/entrepreneurship/ent-start) (in the Practical Entrepreneurship course) for business basics, [Social Media Marketing for local business](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/social-media-marketing/smm-m11) (in the Practical Social Media Marketing course), [Personal Finance investment options](https://naipunyam.github.io/vidhyarambham/#/course/personal-finance/fin-m09) (in the Practical Personal Finance for India course).

## Stay legal

Laws, rates and portals change. Before every deal, check stamp duty and fees, K-RERA rules and tax rules on official sources, and keep your advocate, surveyor and CA in the loop.

sections.title: Glossary with Malayalam terms
sections.summary: 55 key real estate and land-record terms in English and Malayalam.
sections.content:
Key terms, including common Kerala land and document words. Local usage varies between districts and between older and newer documents; if your deeds use a different word, note it next to the entry.

| English | മലയാളം (Malayalam) | Simple meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Cent** | സെന്റ് | One-hundredth of an acre, about 435.6 sq ft (40.47 sq m) |
| **Are** | ആർ | 100 square metres, about 2.47 cents |
| **Hectare** | ഹെക്ടർ | 100 ares, about 2.47 acres |
| **Survey number** | സർവേ നമ്പർ | The number identifying a parcel in survey records |
| **Resurvey number** | റീസർവേ നമ്പർ | The parcel number from the resurvey (block and number) |
| **Thandaper** | തണ്ടപ്പേര് | The landholder's account number in village revenue records |
| **Village office** | വില്ലേജ് ഓഫീസ് | The lowest revenue office, which keeps land records and issues certificates |
| **Land tax** | ഭൂനികുതി / കരം | The annual tax on land paid to the Revenue Department |
| **Possession certificate** | കൈവശ സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് | Village office certificate that a person is in possession of a property |
| **Location certificate** | ലൊക്കേഷൻ സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് | Certificate of where a property is located |
| **Ownership certificate** | ഉടമസ്ഥാവകാശ സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് | Local body certificate of who owns a building |
| **Title deed** | ആധാരം | The registered document that transfers ownership |
| **Prior deeds** | മുന്നാധാരങ്ങൾ | Earlier deeds showing how the property passed to the seller |
| **Encumbrance certificate (EC)** | ബാധ്യതാ സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് (കുടിക്കട സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ്) | Certificate listing registered transactions on a property for a period |
| **Mutation** | പോക്കുവരവ് | Changing the owner's name in revenue records after a transfer |
| **Sketch / FMB** | സ്കെച്ച് / എഫ്.എം.ബി. | Survey map of a parcel showing boundaries and measurements |
| **Purayidam (dry land)** | പുരയിടം | Garden or dry land, generally usable for houses |
| **Nilam (wet land / paddy land)** | നിലം | Paddy or wet land, protected by law |
| **Data bank** | ഡാറ്റാ ബാങ്ക് | The official list of paddy and wetlands under the 2008 Act |
| **Puramboke** | പുറമ്പോക്ക് | Government land not assigned to anyone (roadsides, river banks) |
| **Pattayam** | പട്ടയം | A government grant of land to a person |
| **Sub-Registrar Office (SRO)** | സബ് രജിസ്ട്രാർ ഓഫീസ് | The office where property documents are registered |
| **Document writer** | ആധാരം എഴുത്തുകാരൻ | A licensed professional who drafts deeds |
| **Stamp duty** | മുദ്രവില | Tax paid to the state on a document such as a sale deed |
| **Registration fee** | രജിസ്ട്രേഷൻ ഫീസ് | Fee paid to register a document |
| **Fair value** | ന്യായവില | The government-notified minimum land value used for stamp duty |
| **Market value** | വിപണി വില | The price a willing buyer and seller agree on |
| **Token advance** | ടോക്കൺ അഡ്വാൻസ് | A small first payment to hold a deal |
| **Agreement for sale** | വിൽപ്പന കരാർ | A contract promising a future sale; does not transfer ownership |
| **Sale deed** | വിലയാധാരം | The registered document transferring ownership for a price |
| **Gift deed** | ദാനാധാരം | A registered transfer without payment |
| **Settlement deed** | ഒഴിമുറി / ധനനിശ്ചയാധാരം | A registered transfer, usually within a family, with conditions |
| **Partition deed** | ഭാഗപത്രം | A registered division of jointly owned property |
| **Power of attorney** | മുക്ത്യാർ | A document authorising someone to act for another |
| **Release deed** | ഒഴിവുകുറി | A document giving up a share or right in property |
| **Mortgage** | പണയം | Property pledged as security for a loan |
| **Building permit** | കെട്ടിട നിർമ്മാണ പെർമിറ്റ് | Local body permission to construct |
| **Occupancy certificate** | ഒക്യുപൻസി സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് | Local body certificate that a building can be used |
| **Building number** | കെട്ടിട നമ്പർ | The number a local body assigns to a building |
| **Building tax** | കെട്ടിട നികുതി | The property tax on buildings paid to the local body |
| **NOC** | നിരാക്ഷേപ പത്രം | No objection certificate from an authority |
| **Access road** | വഴി | The road or path to the property; legal right of way matters |
| **Encroachment** | കയ്യേറ്റം | Unlawful occupation of someone else's or government land |
| **Commission / brokerage** | കമ്മീഷൻ / ബ്രോക്കറേജ് | The fee paid to an agent |
| **Mandate** | അധികാരപത്രം | Written authority from an owner to market a property |
| **Rental agreement** | വാടക കരാർ | Contract between landlord and tenant |
| **Security deposit** | സുരക്ഷാ നിക്ഷേപം | Refundable money held by the landlord |
| **Rental yield** | വാടക ആദായം | Annual rent as a percentage of the price |
| **Capital gains** | മൂലധന നേട്ടം | Profit on selling a capital asset such as property |
| **TDS** | ഉറവിടത്തിൽ നികുതി പിടിക്കൽ | Tax deducted at source by the buyer and paid to the government |
| **Benami property** | ബിനാമി സ്വത്ത് | Property held in another person's name while someone else paid and benefits |
| **Layout** | ലേഔട്ട് | A plan dividing land into plots with roads |
| **CRZ** | തീരദേശ പരിപാലന മേഖല | Coastal Regulation Zone, where building is restricted |
| **ESA** | പരിസ്ഥിതി ലോല പ്രദേശം | Ecologically sensitive area |
| **REIT** | റിയൽ എസ്റ്റേറ്റ് നിക്ഷേപ ട്രസ്റ്റ് | A listed trust that owns income-producing property |

sections.content:
Every link in the course with where it is used and when it was checked (2026-11-04).

- **verified:** the page was opened and matched what the course says.
- **verified; check current rules:** the page was checked, but it describes something that changes (a rate, a fee, a rule, a portal).
- **verified through a secondary source:** the figure was checked on a reputable secondary guide, not the official page. Confirm on the official source before relying on it.
- **unverified:** the official site blocks automated checks (most Kerala Registration and Revenue portals do), or the address came only from a search. Type the address yourself and check you are on the real government site (it ends in **.gov.in**).

No law, section number, rate or statistic in this course was written from memory without a check; where a check wasn't possible the point is described in general terms and marked "check current rules".
